Tier 1 System Context Diagram

This is the Tier 1 Context view of TothBot V2 — the system-level overview that serves as parent for every Tier 2 diagram in this document (Diagrams 1-7). It depicts the TothBot V2 organism (KRAKEN role + TOTHBOT role + CIATS role per TB00000 §1) and its primary external actors / boundaries: Bill (sole operator), Hetzner VPS (hosting boundary), Mail Alerts (alert delivery via alerts@tothbot.com), GitHub Repositories (source-of-truth), and the external Kraken Exchange infrastructure (Public WS v2 + Private WS v2 + REST).

The PA-001 banner at the top encodes the paper-as-master direction-of-mimicry visually: paper trading IS the master configuration; live trading mimics paper byte-identically EXCEPT at the four PA-004 divergence points (Private WS, order dispatch, capital ledger, Position Mirror sourcing). Red arrows mark the PA-004 divergence flows; blue arrows mark byte-identical paper / live flows; gray arrows mark operational channels (Bill / VPS / GitHub / Mail).

Tier 1 RULE: this diagram has parent_diagram = none (it is itself the root). Every labeled <g> group in this diagram carries class="tier-1" and a structured <title>+<desc> per 0311001 v1_7 §15.11.6 (Tier 1 root-desc contract — added in this dv1_25 amendment cycle bundled with TB00154 Stage A). The seven drill_target attributes in the root <desc> resolve to the seven Tier 2 diagrams (D1 - D7) below.

1. System Identity and Mission

1.1 What TothBot Is

TothBot is an automated cryptocurrency spot trading system on Kraken exchange. It runs
24/7/365 on a Hetzner VPS, processes 5-minute OHLC candle close events as its system
clock, and executes long-only trades using a momentum-based signal engine.

TothBot is not an external system connected to Kraken — it IS Kraken's event processor.
Every action is a response to a Kraken push event. No timers. No polling. Idle and silent
until Kraken speaks.

1.2 The One Organism Principle

Three functional zones, one organism:
Kraken: generates events, executes orders, holds resting TP limit orders and
off-book emergency SL stop orders on matching engine
TothBot: processes Kraken events, executes trading strategy, manages positions
CIATS: learns from event records, continuously improves processing rules

PRIMARY MISSION: Maximize profit. Minimize loss. With an emphasis on minimizing loss.
Loss prevention takes priority over profit generation. Everything else is secondary.

1.3 Operating Environment 

  Exchange:          Kraken Spot (Long_Module) + Kraken Margin (Short_Module)
                     — parallel-module framework supporting Long_Module,
                     Short_Module, and future trading modules (per TB00000
                     v2_29 §9.3; diagrams remain canonical per §4.5 DD-001/
                     DD-002 + 0311001 v1_12 §15.14)
  Language:          Python 3.12.3
  VPS:               Hetzner CPX22 — 87.99.141.44 — Ashburn VA
                     (Kraken Spot servers: AWS us-west-2 Oregon)
                     ★ Evaluate Hillsboro OR [dv1_6 IMP-01 — adjacent to Kraken AWS]
  System Clock:      Kraken OHLC 5-minute candle close event (WS v2 push)
  Fee Baseline:      Maker 0.16% / Taker 0.26% (CIATS monitors actuals)
  Operation:         24/7/365 — CIATS may add stand-down periods via PDCA if data supports
  Paper-Trading      Operator-funded per-module, affordable-loss capital (primary loss control):
  Wallets:               paper_starting_balance_long_usd  = $5,000  (Long_Module)
                         paper_starting_balance_short_usd = $5,000  (Short_Module)
                     Live-trading wallet funding is a separate Bill decision informed by
                     paper-trading results. Per TB00000 v2_29 §9.4.
  Sacred constraint: Net 1:1.5 R:R MINIMUM floor on every trade — HARDCODED — the only

2. Kraken API Connection Architecture

2.0 Canonical Identifiers (NEW dv1_37 — V-038.3 reconciliation per DR-042; DD-002 prose-follows-diagram). The pair_cache architectural element narrated in this section (and cross-referenced in §3 Trading Pipeline + §11 Trade Lifecycle) resolves to canonical-token form pair_cache per 0311001 §15.11.3. WS Manager owns and maintains pair_cache as the authoritative pair-spec source; all consumers (Selection Controller, Long Module, Position Mirror) read from pair_cache via startup injection per ar:AR-073 + rule:HR-EC-014. Encoded in D1 Kraken API Connection Architecture across 6 SVG sites.

All connection points verified across 3 independent analysis passes (15 sources) plus
2 deep validation sessions (144+ sources total) plus 10-search FP/DP Kraken validation
[dv1_6] (126 sources).

2.1 Key Connection Points 

  Public WS v2:
    instrument  — asset specs + per-pair status cache ★ dv1_6
                  price_increment / qty_min / cost_min ★ GAP-C/D dv1_9
    status      — global engine state (online/post_only/cancel_only/maintenance)
    ohlc(5m)    — SYSTEM CLOCK (pipeline trigger, fires on trade events)
    ohlc(60)    — 1H HTF cache for Gate 4 ★ NEW dv1_5
    ticker      — price data, event_trigger:bbo (pairs with open positions) or
                  event_trigger:trades (pairs without). WS Manager manages per-pair.

  Private WS v2 inbound:
    executions  — fills/expirations/SL-TP triggers, ratecounter:true (A-1),
                  snap_orders:true, snap_trades:true, order_status:true on reconnect (A-3),
                  sequence gap detection ★ A-10 dv1_7
                  CRITICAL ★ GAP-A dv1_9: order_status:true MANDATORY — without it amended
                  and restated exec_types are silently dropped, breaking A-12 and A-13
    balances    — real-time settlement, sequence gap detection ★ A-9 dv1_6

  Private WS v2 outbound:
    add_order   — entry: limit/post_only/GTD/cl_ord_id/stp_type:cancel_newest/deadline:now+5s
    amend_order — PRIMARY amendment method (edit_order DEPRECATED ★ dv1_6)
    batch_add   — SL+TP atomic on fill. cl_ord_id/stp_type:cancel_newest/deadline:now+5s
    cancel_order — exit leg cleanup, req_id tracked
    batch_cancel — Full Halt multi-order cancel ★ dv1_6
    All messages carry req_id (A-2), cl_ord_id (A-2), stp_type:cancel_newest (A-4) [WS v2 underscore]

  REST:
    GetWebSocketsToken  — startup/reconnect
    GetOHLCData         — daily regime computation 00:00 UTC ★ NEW dv1_5
                          CRITICAL: exclude response[-1] always ★ dv1_6
    GetOpenOrders       — restart reconcile fallback / executions gap recovery ★ dv1_7
    GetAccountBalance   — restart reconcile fallback / balances gap recovery ★ dv1_6
    CancelAllOrders     — kill switch emergency only
    Status API          — startup proactive maintenance check (AR-038 dv1_12)
                          GET https://status.kraken.com/api/v2/
                          scheduled-maintenances/upcoming.json
                          No authentication. Informational only. Does not block startup.

  Matching Engine:
    Resting TP limit orders and off-book emergency SL stop orders survive any TothBot
    failure independently — crash protection always active

  EVALUATED AND REJECTED:
    cancel_all_orders_after (WS v2 DMS) — destroys crash protection (AR-001)
    FIX API cancel-on-disconnect — same architectural conflict (AR-001)
    OTO conditional orders — uses limit price not fill price, violates R:R (AR-008)

2.2 Four Kraken Engine States 

  online       — All orders. Signal pipeline runs normally.
  post_only    — TothBot limit+post_only entries ARE valid. Trading continues.
  cancel_only  — No new entries. Exit Controller can cancel. Resting orders active.
  maintenance  — No orders, no cancels. Resting TP and emergSL active on engine.

2.3 API Rate Limits — Intermediate Tier (C-2) 

  Rate limits shared across REST, WebSockets, and FIX — no separate per-protocol budget.

  Rate counter threshold (per pair):   125
  Rate counter decay (per second):      2.34
  Max open orders (per pair):          80
  Add order fixed cost:                +1
  Amend order cost ★ dv1_6 (PRIMARY): +1 fixed, +3(<5s), +2(<10s), +1(<15s)
  Edit order (DEPRECATED ★ dv1_6):    +1 fixed, +6(<5s), +5(<10s) — DO NOT USE
  Batch add fixed cost:                +(n/2)
  Cancel order cost (< 5s old):        +8
  Cancel order cost (< 10s old):       +6
  Cancel order cost (< 300s old):      +1
  Batch cancel cost ★ dv1_6:          Cumulative sum of individual order cancel costs

  amend_order is 43% cheaper than edit_order for orders resting <5s (+4 vs +7).
  amend_order preserves queue position (unlike cancel+resubmit).

2.4 WS Operational Requirements (A-1 through A-10)

A-1 Rate counter monitoring via executions channel:
executions subscription accepts ratecounter:true. Real-time rate counter per pair
included at zero additional connection cost. CIATS EWMA Monitor adds
rate_counter_by_pair as third monitoring signal. Assign to 0511003 and 0211001.

A-2 req_id and cl_ord_id on all outbound WS messages:
All outbound messages carry req_id (client-specified integer). All add_order and
batch_add additionally carry cl_ord_id (up to 18 characters). TothBot assigns
cl_ord_id at dispatch time before Kraken response. Position Mirror records cl_ord_id
immediately at dispatch — no async gap. WS Manager maintains pending-request registry. cl_ord_id and req_id MUST each be unique per outstanding order - they are the correlation keys used to bind acknowledgements and fills to the originating order, so a collision misattributes a fill. The uniqueness-achieving construction scheme (e.g. symbol prefix + millisecond timestamp) is an implementation choice, not architecture (dv1_141; TB00511).
Assign to 0511001, 0511003, 0511005.

A-3 Round-trip latency monitoring and WS reconciliation:
All WS v2 responses include time_in and time_out to nanosecond precision. Logger
records these fields. CIATS EWMA Monitor adds ws_roundtrip_latency_ms. executions
channel supports snap_orders:true on subscription — preferred over REST GetOpenOrders
for restart reconciliation. Assign to 0511001, 0511006, 0211001.

A-4 stp_type:cancel_newest on all WS v2 add_order and batch_add calls:
All add_order and batch_add include stp_type:cancel_newest [WS v2 underscore format].
REST API uses cancel-newest [hyphen] — different protocols, different formats (A-20).
Self Trade Prevention prevents TothBot from inadvertently filling against its own
resting orders.

A-5 Reconnect behavior distinction:
(1) Random drop: reconnect instantly, up to a handful of attempts.
(2) After confirmed trading engine maintenance: minimum 5-second delay.
Both implemented as separate paths in WS Manager. Assign to 0511001.

A-6 (dv1_5) OTO conditional orders — REJECTED:
OTO uses limit price not actual fill price — violates sacred R:R. Creates Position
Mirror race condition. batch_add on fill confirmed correct. See AR-008.

A-7 (dv1_6) ★ WS Ping / Keepalive Strategy:
Kraken WS server disconnects after ~60 seconds of inactivity. Cloudflare idle
timeout ~100 seconds. WS Manager MUST send {"method":"ping"} on each active
connection every 30 seconds. Expects {"method":"pong"} within 10 seconds. No pong
within 10 seconds = dead connection. Reconnect immediately. Application-level ping,
distinct from TCP keepalive. Assign to 0511001, 1011002.

A-8 (dv1_6) ★ Zombie Connection Detection:
A WS connection can appear alive (ping/pong passing) while delivering no real market
data. WS Manager MUST track last_real_data_time per connection using time.monotonic().
Only actual market data events reset this timestamp — heartbeat messages alone do NOT.
If elapsed > 90 seconds: log ZOMBIE_CONNECTION_DETECTED, alert operator, reconnect.
Assign to 0511001, 1011002.

A-9 (dv1_6) ★ Balances Channel Sequence Gap Detection:
Every balances channel message carries a sequence integer. WS Manager MUST track
last-seen sequence. Any gap (skip > 1) indicates a missed ledger event. On gap:
alert immediately, trigger REST GetAccountBalance reconciliation. Missed balance
events cause incorrect available capital calculation — direct loss risk.
Assign to 0511001, 1011002.

A-10 (dv1_7) ★ Executions Channel Sequence Gap Detection:
Every executions channel message carries a sequence integer. WS Manager MUST track
last-seen sequence independently of balances. Any gap (skip > 1) indicates missed
order/fill events. On gap: alert immediately, trigger REST GetOpenOrders reconciliation
to restore Position Mirror accuracy. Missed execution events mean TothBot does not know
a position is open or closed — direct loss risk. Higher severity than A-9 (balances):
a missed fill leaves Position Mirror in stale state; the next pipeline evaluation
operates on incorrect position data. Sequence tracking resets on each new subscription
(reconnect). Do not gap-detect across sessions.
Assign to 0511001, 1011002.

A-11 (dv1_8) ★ Executions Channel: cancel_reason Deprecated — Use reason Field:
The cancel_reason field in executions channel events is DEPRECATED since WS v2.0.0
(December 2023). All code parsing cancellation events MUST read msg["reason"], not
msg["cancel_reason"]. cancel_reason returns None on all modern messages. Silent
reason loss corrupts CIATS EWMA rejection_rate_by_regime monitoring accuracy.
Assign to 1011002 WM-EXE-002 through WM-EXE-004.

A-12 (dv1_8) ★ Executions Channel: Complete exec_type Enum Handling Required:
WS Manager MUST handle all exec_type values: pending_new, new, trade, filled,
iceberg_refill, canceled, expired, amended, restated, status. Using a partial
dispatch table causes unknown exec_type events to silently fall through. Use
handle_exec_unknown for unrecognized values — log full payload, never silently ignore.
TothBot primary events: trade (trigger batch_add), filled, expired (log GTD expiry),
canceled (log with reason). amended and restated: log only, no Position Mirror change.
Assign to 1011002 WM-EXE-005 through WM-EXE-007.

A-13 (dv1_8) ★ Executions Channel: restated exec_type Must Not Trigger Position Change:
restated fires when Kraken's matching engine amends an order for maintenance purposes.
It is NOT a fill, NOT a cancel, NOT a user action. On restated: (1) log with reason
field, (2) alert operator (informational), (3) do NOT update Position Mirror, (4) if
the restated order is a resting TP or emergSL, escalate to HIGH severity alert and
queue a reconciliation check on the next pipeline cycle. The restated event on a
resting crash-protection order indicates Kraken modified our stop — must be visible.
Assign to 1011002 WM-EXE-008 through WM-EXE-010.

A-14 (dv1_8) ★ Spot REST Authentication: Confirmed Unchanged — PL-014 RESOLVED:
The October 1, 2025 authentication breaking change applied to Futures REST ONLY.
Kraken Spot REST authentication is UNCHANGED: HMAC-SHA512 of (URI path + SHA256
(nonce + POST data)) using base64-decoded secret. No code changes required.
PL-014 is fully resolved. No Bill verification action required.
Assign to 0411001 WS-AUTH-001 through WS-AUTH-003.

A-15 (dv1_9) ★ Executions Channel: order_status:true MANDATORY — GAP-A CRITICAL FIX:
Without order_status:true in the executions subscription, the channel only delivers:
new, filled, canceled, expired. The exec_types amended and restated are SILENTLY DROPPED.
This means: (1) A-13 restated protection for crash-protection orders is completely non-
functional without this flag — the restated event never arrives. (2) A-12 dispatch table
handles 10 exec_types but receives only 4. The subscription is already specified correctly
(WS-EXE-001 in 0411001) but this architectural consequence must be explicitly documented.
Assign to 0411001 WS-OSTA-001 through WS-OSTA-003, 1011002 WM-EXE-011/-012.

A-16 (dv1_9) ★ OHLC Channel: interval_begin Replaces Deprecated timestamp — GAP-B:
The Kraken WS v2 OHLC channel deprecated the timestamp field. Subscription ACK warns:
"timestamp is deprecated, use interval_begin". TothBot MUST parse interval_begin
(RFC3339 nanosecond string) as the candle start time, not timestamp.
Assign to 0411001 WS-OHLC-002 through -005, 1011002 WM-OHLC-001 through -003.

A-17 (dv1_9) ★ Instrument Channel: price_increment / qty_min / cost_min — GAP-C/D:
(GAP-C) The instrument channel deprecated tick_size. Use price_increment exclusively.
Subscription ACK warns: "tick_size is deprecated, use price_increment".
(GAP-D) The instrument channel provides qty_min (minimum order quantity) and cost_min
(minimum order cost = price × qty). Gate 8 Position Sizer MUST validate both before
submitting any add_order. Violation causes immediate order rejection.
Assign to 0411001 WS-INST-001 through -007, 1011002 WM-INST-001 through -005.

A-18 (dv1_9) ★ WebSocket Library max_size = 10MB — GAP-E:
Python websockets library default max_size = 1MB. The Kraken instrument channel
snapshot for 500+ pairs can exceed 1MB, causing PayloadTooBig and silent disconnect.
All WS connect() calls MUST set max_size=10*1024*1024 (10MB) and open_timeout=10.
Assign to 0411001 WS-LIB-001 through -003, 1011002 WM-LIB-001 through -003.

A-19 (dv1_9) ★ maxratecount from Executions ACK is Operative Rate Threshold — IMP-11:
The executions subscription ACK returns maxratecount — the actual operative rate
counter ceiling for this user tier. TothBot MUST extract and use maxratecount as the
operative threshold for all rate counter monitoring, not the hardcoded value 125.
If tier changes, maxratecount automatically updates on next reconnect.
Assign to 0411001 WS-RL-003, WS-EXEC-001a, 1011002 WM-RATE-001 through -003.

A-20 (dv1_10) ★ stp_type Format CORRECTION — WS v2 Uses Underscore, Not Hyphen:
Official Kraken WS v2 documentation and batch_add examples use underscore format:
cancel_newest, cancel_oldest, cancel_both
REST API uses hyphen format: cancel-newest, cancel-oldest, cancel-both.
These are DIFFERENT protocols with DIFFERENT formats. All WS v2 outbound messages
(add_order, batch_add) MUST use the underscore format. Using the hyphen format in
WS v2 will cause order rejection or silent failure. This was an error in all
prior dv1_9 and earlier specifications. Corrected here as AR-032.
Assign to 0411001 WS-STP-001 through -003, 1011002 WM-STP-001 through -003.

A-21 (dv1_10) ★ deadline Parameter on All WS v2 Order Submissions:
Both add_order and batch_add support a deadline parameter: an ISO 8601 UTC
timestamp string. The engine rejects any order arriving after this time.
Valid range: 500ms to 60 seconds from current time. Default: 5 seconds.
TothBot standard: deadline = current UTC time + 5 seconds.
Provides protection against stale order placement due to network delay or
event loop pauses. Without deadline, a delayed add_order could place an entry
at a price that has already moved adversely.
CRITICAL: deadline also applies to batch_add. A delayed batch_add with incorrect
TP/emergSL prices due to fill price slippage is prevented by deadline enforcement.
Generate: deadline = (datetime.utcnow() + timedelta(seconds=5)).strftime(
'%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f')[:-3] + 'Z'
Assign to 0411001 WS-DL-001 through -004, 1011002 WM-DL-001 through -004.

A-22 (dv1_10) ★ aiohttp ClientSession Timeout and Connector Configuration:
All REST calls use a single shared aiohttp.ClientSession with explicit timeout and
connector configuration. Without explicit timeout, REST calls can hang indefinitely
if Kraken REST servers become unresponsive. This blocks the asyncio event loop
for aiohttp operations and starves other tasks.
Required configuration:
timeout = aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=10, connect=5, sock_read=8)
connector = aiohttp.TCPConnector(limit=10, limit_per_host=5, force_close=False)
session = aiohttp.ClientSession(timeout=timeout, connector=connector)
total=10: maximum 10 seconds for complete request (connect + send + read).
connect=5: maximum 5 seconds to establish TCP connection.
sock_read=8: maximum 8 seconds waiting for server response after sending.
force_close=False: enables HTTP keepalive — connection reused across calls.
Assign to 1011002 WM-REST-006 through -011, 1011001 BP-HTTP-001 through -004.

A-23 (dv1_10) ★ Ticker event_trigger per Position State:
The ticker channel event_trigger parameter controls when updates are published.
event_trigger:bbo — fires on every change to best bid or ask price.
event_trigger:trades — fires only when a trade occurs (matching engine event).
For pairs WITH open positions: use event_trigger:bbo.
Rationale: For long positions, the bid price is the realizable exit price.
bbo fires immediately when the bid drops, giving the Exit Controller maximum
reaction time to detect MAE threshold breach. trades-only can miss bid drops
that occur without a matching trade.
For pairs WITHOUT open positions: use event_trigger:trades.
Rationale: Reduces unnecessary event volume. Signal pipeline uses last price
not bid, so trades trigger is sufficient for scoring.
WS Manager adjusts per-pair event_trigger when Position Mirror changes state.
Implementation: re-subscribe ticker for that pair with updated event_trigger.
Assign to 0411001 WS-TKR-001 through -004, 1011002 WM-TKR-001 through -004.

A-24 (dv1_10) ★ Regime Engine GetOHLCData Rate Limit Staggering:
REST public GetOHLCData is rate-limited by IP address + currency pair at 1/second.
Calling it for all monitored pairs simultaneously at 00:00 UTC triggers rate limits.
All GetOHLCData calls in the Regime Engine MUST be staggered with asyncio.sleep(1.1)
between each pair to stay below the rate limit ceiling.
Example for 50 pairs: 50 × 1.1s = 55s total. Completes well before first 5m candle
of the new day (~05:00 UTC for the first significant candle after the daily open).
On rate limit error (HTTP 429): exponential backoff, log REGIME_OHLC_RATE_LIMITED,
retry up to 3 times. If all fail: use stale regime (per RE-SCH-004).
1011012 RE-RL-001 through -004 retired TB00227; 0711002 retired TB00596 — canonical authority is the Diagram 4 regime-engine visual / §5 (see 0500000 dv1_55 §12.5 Bind block).

2.5 Data Architecture: Pre-Computation Cache (NEW dv1_5 — I-2)

HOT PATH RULE: The 5-minute pipeline hot path reads cached values ONLY. No computation
occurs during pipeline evaluation. All indicators maintained as incremental running
calculations updated on each event trigger.

IMP-06 (dv1_8) ★ aiohttp Mandatory for All REST Calls:
All Kraken REST calls MUST use aiohttp (async HTTP). Never use the requests library
inside asyncio — it blocks the event loop during the entire call duration. Create one
aiohttp.ClientSession at TothBot startup, reuse for all REST calls, close at shutdown.
Assign to 1011002 WM-REST-001 through WM-REST-005.

IMP-07 (dv1_8) ★ asyncio TaskManager Pattern — Mandatory for 24/7 Operation:
All asyncio.create_task() calls MUST store a strong reference AND register a done
callback via task.add_done_callback(task_set.discard). Failure to do so causes memory
leaks in long-running processes: the task set grows indefinitely until OOM. All task
creation routed through a central create_task() helper function. Long-running tasks
(ping, zombie, watchdog) stored as named instance variables, cancelled and awaited
explicitly during reconnect cleanup.
Assign to 1011002 WM-TASK-001 through WM-TASK-004.

IMP-08 (dv1_8) ★ systemd Watchdog Integration — Frozen Process Detection:
TothBot MUST run as a systemd service with WatchdogSec=120 and Type=notify. A
separate asyncio.Task pings systemd sd_notify every 30 seconds via WATCHDOG=1
message. If the event loop hangs (frozen process), the watchdog stops, systemd
detects no ping within 120s, and restarts TothBot. Without this, a frozen-but-alive
TothBot with open positions is undetected indefinitely.
Assign to 0211002 IN-PM-003 + 0211002 IN-PM-004 + D7 systemd-tier visual cluster (per DD-001 diagrams-canonical; 1011013 dv1_6 retired in TB00228 RANK 7 cascade).

IMP-16 (dv1_10) ★ aiohttp ClientSession Timeout — Required for REST Reliability:
All REST calls via aiohttp MUST use explicit timeout and connector configuration.
Without explicit timeout, a degraded Kraken REST server causes asyncio tasks to
hang indefinitely, blocking reconnect/gap recovery sequences.
ClientTimeout(total=10, connect=5, sock_read=8) applied at session creation.
See A-22 for full specification. Assign to 1011002 WM-REST-006 through -011.

IMP-17 (dv1_10) ★ aiohttp TCPConnector for Connection Reuse:
TCPConnector(limit=10, limit_per_host=5, force_close=False) enables HTTP keepalive.
Without this, aiohttp closes the TCP connection after every REST call and re-opens
it on the next call. For GetWebSocketsToken (called every reconnect) and
GetOpenOrders (called on gap detection), connection reuse materially reduces latency.
See A-22 for full specification. Assign to 1011002 WM-REST-009 through -011.

IMP-18 (dv1_10) ★ Ticker event_trigger:bbo for Open Position MAE Detection:
Pairs with open positions MUST use event_trigger:bbo on ticker subscription.
bbo fires immediately on any best bid/ask price change — not just on trades.
For long positions, bid = realizable exit price. bbo maximizes Layer 2 exit
detection speed. Pairs without open positions use event_trigger:trades.
See A-23 for full specification. Assign to 0411001, 1011002.

IMP-19 (dv1_10) ★ Regime Engine REST Rate Limit Stagger Required:
All GetOHLCData calls in the Regime Engine must use asyncio.sleep(1.1) between
pairs to stay within public REST rate limits. Without stagger, simultaneous calls
for 50+ pairs at 00:00 UTC hit the rate limit and corrupt regime classification
for all affected pairs. See A-24. 1011012 RE-RL-001 through -004 retired TB00227; 0711002 retired TB00596 — canonical authority is the Diagram 4 regime-engine visual / §5 (see 0500000 dv1_55 §12.5 Bind block).

A-25 (dv1_144) ★ Keepalive, Sequence-Gap Recovery, and Connection Logging (DD-002 prose-follows-diagram for the D1 mod:WS_Manager dv1_144 migration; TB00532):
The diagram mod:WS_Manager constraints <desc> is canonical for these wire facts (SD-9-verified vs 0411001 dv1_13):
(i) Dead-connection: a sent application ping that receives no Kraken pong within 10 seconds marks the connection dead and forces reconnect [WS-PING-002, 0411001 L980-981].
(ii) Zombie detection: WS Manager tracks last_real_data_time per connection; if time.monotonic() minus last_real_data_time exceeds 90 seconds the connection is a zombie — log ZOMBIE_CONNECTION_DETECTED and reconnect [WS-ZOM-003, 0411001 L1008-1011].
(iii) Executions sequence gap: on a sequence jump greater than 1 on the executions stream, alert EXECUTIONS_SEQUENCE_GAP immediately and trigger a REST GetOpenOrders reconciliation [WS-EXE-019, 0411001 L576-578] — prevents Position Mirror desync.
(iv) Balances sequence gap: on a sequence jump greater than 1 on the balances stream, alert BALANCES_SEQUENCE_GAP immediately and trigger a REST balance reconciliation [WS-BAL-005, 0411001 L607-608] — prevents capital-calculation error.
(v) Connection logging: log connection_id on every new WS connection as WS_CONNECTED(uri, connection_id); connection_id enables Kraken support diagnosis [WS-STAT-006, 0411001 L289-292].

A-26 (dv1_144) ★ Exit Controller Pair-Status Adaptation (DD-002 prose-follows-diagram for the D1 mod:Exit_Controller dv1_144 migration; TB00532):
The diagram mod:Exit_Controller constraints <desc> is canonical (WS-EXIT-003; SD-9-verified vs 0411001 dv1_13 sec 9): the Exit Controller adapts exit-order placement to the live Kraken pair trading-status — limit_only places an IOC/GTC limit order only and never a market order [L228/L1103]; cancel_only cancels resting orders only and places no new orders [L230/L264]; reduce_only / work_in_progress / maintenance / delisted follow the sec-9 pair-status adaptation matrix [L236-237]. Submitting a non-permitted order type under a restricted pair-status is Kraken-rejected and would leave an open position unprotected (loss-prevention: wrong-exit-mode loss).

A-27 (dv1_145) ★ Public Market Data: Pair/Engine Status, OHLC, and Ticker (DD-002 prose-follows-diagram for the D1 mod:WS_Manager dv1_145 migration; TB00533):
The diagram mod:WS_Manager constraints <desc> is canonical for the four public market-data channels (GROUP 2 wire facts, SD-9-verified vs 0411001 dv1_13). INSTRUMENT/STATUS: the instrument channel reports a pair trading-status with 8 states (online, post_only, limit_only, reduce_only, cancel_only, work_in_progress, maintenance, delisted [WS-INST-008]); of these, six — cancel_only, work_in_progress, delisted, limit_only, reduce_only, maintenance — are the NO-ENTRY set that blocks all new entry orders, so only online and post_only pairs are entry-eligible [WS-INST-009; AR-039]. The status channel additionally reports 4 GLOBAL engine states (online / post_only / cancel_only / maintenance) to which WS_Manager reacts immediately on change [WS-STAT-002], and carries a connection_id field identifying the specific WS connection [WS-STAT-005] — the value the WS-STAT-006 mandatory connection log records. OHLC: two ohlc subscriptions are maintained at startup for every monitored pair — interval=5 (the 5-minute SYSTEM CLOCK) and interval=60 (1-hour HTF Gate 4) [WS-OHLC-001]; interval_begin is the canonical candle-start field and timestamp is DEPRECATED (parse only interval_begin) [WS-OHLC-002; AR-027], formatted as an RFC3339 nanosecond string parsed to a timezone-aware datetime [WS-OHLC-003]. TICKER: the ticker event_trigger has two modes — bbo for pairs WITH an open position (faster adverse-price detection; for longs the bid is the realizable exit price) and trades for pairs WITHOUT a position (sufficient for the Gate-2 24h-volume read) [WS-TKR-002] — and WS_Manager switches a pair's event_trigger on every position-state change (opened → bbo, closed → trades) [WS-TKR-003]. These nine facts are TothBot-organism (Kraken event-source) architecture per the binary test and are now derivable from the D1 diagram alone (DD-014); R holds at R10 (a <desc>-only edit).

A-28 (dv1_146) ★ Private-Channel Inbound: exec_type Enumeration, Partial-Fill Fields, and Spot/Main Balance Merge (DD-002 prose-follows-diagram for the D1 mod:WS_Manager dv1_146 migration; TB00535):
The diagram mod:WS_Manager constraints <desc> is canonical for the Kraken private-channel inbound wire facts (GROUP 3, SD-9-verified vs 0411001 dv1_13). The executions channel reports a 10-value exec_type dispatch table (pending_new, new, trade, filled, iceberg_refill, canceled, expired, amended, restated, status) all handled explicitly with unknown values logged WARN [WS-EXE-009]; exec_type=trade fires on every partial fill of an entry or TP order and does not imply a full fill [WS-EXE-011]; and each trade event carries cum_qty + avg_price (consumed by Position Mirror and R:R sizing) plus last_qty + last_price (fill-level / slippage analytics) [WS-EXE-012]. The balances channel is filtered to wallets[type=spot][id=main] ONLY — futures and staking balances are never included in portfolio calculations [WS-BAL-002] — and is parsed as a full snapshot at subscription followed by delta updates merged into the cached spot/main balance [WS-BAL-003]. These five facts are TothBot-organism (Kraken event-source) architecture per the binary test and are now derivable from the D1 diagram alone (DD-014); R holds at R10 (a <desc>-only edit).

A-29 (dv1_147) ★ Outbound Orders: deadline Range, Entry GTD Expiry, amend_order Queue-Position Preservation, batch_add TP/emergSL Template, and Partial-TP emergSL Amendment (DD-002 prose-follows-diagram for the D1 mod:WS_Manager + mod:Exit_Controller dv1_147 migration; TB00536):
The diagram mod:WS_Manager and mod:Exit_Controller constraints <desc> are canonical for the Kraken outbound-order wire facts (GROUP 4, SD-9-verified vs 0411001 dv1_13). The deadline field on every add_order and batch_add accepts a 500ms-to-60s range from current time, with TothBot using the 5s standard value; an order whose deadline has passed at processing time is Kraken-rejected, preventing stale entry placement from network delay or event-loop pause [WS-DL-002]. Entry orders are MARKETABLE IOC LIMIT orders (time_in_force=ioc, marketable limit price) bounded by a maximum-permissible-price (MPP) slippage cap on the worst acceptable fill; any unfilled IOC remainder expires immediately, so there is no resting working entry order and no entry-side dust; the MPP cap is the CIATS-owned bound and the architecture fact is the marketable-IOC-with-MPP-cap contract, not a seed value (the legacy GTD param:entry_timeout_sec seed is obviated under IOC; sec 9.17 disposition is DEC-122 CR-17) [WS-ADD-002; DEC-122 CR-03]. amend_order preserves the order's queue position on the Kraken book whereas cancel+resubmit loses it, which is why amend_order is the sole modification method (ar:AR-018; edit_order DEPRECATED) and the preferred mechanism under rate-limit pressure [WS-AMD-002]. The batch_add fired atomically on entry fill carries two legs: a TP leg (limit, sell, post_only:true — post_only guarantees the maker fee on the TP exit, since a taker TP fill would violate the fee baseline assumed by the Sacred 1:1.5 R:R floor) and an emergSL leg (stop-loss, triggers.reference='last', triggers.price_type='static' for a fixed-price crash-protection stop that must be set explicitly), both with stp_type=cancel_newest and deadline [WS-BA-002]. On a partial TP fill the Exit Controller computes remaining_qty = tp_order_qty - cum_qty and amend_orders the resting emergSL down to remaining_qty (preserving its queue position); if the remainder falls below qty_min or cost_min it is sub-minimum and cannot be sold on Kraken Spot, so per DR-079 the Exit Controller cancels the emergSL and ABANDONS the sub-minimum remainder as bounded dust, surfacing it for periodic manual Convert Small Balances (abandon-and-surface, NOT a market-sell) [WS-TP-003; DR-079; DEC-122 CR-05]. These facts are TothBot-organism (Kraken event-source) architecture per the binary test and are now derivable from the D1 diagram alone (DD-014); R holds at R10 (a <desc>-only edit).

A-30 (dv1_148) ★ Reconnect Residual: Scenario B Maintenance-Delay and the On-Reconnect Restore Sequence (DD-002 prose-follows-diagram for the D1 mod:WS_Manager dv1_148 GROUP 5 migration; TB00537):
The diagram mod:WS_Manager constraints <desc> is canonical for the two remaining Kraken keepalive/reconnect wire facts (GROUP 5 residual, SD-9-verified vs 0411001 dv1_13). Reconnection has two distinct behaviours: Scenario A (a random disconnect) reconnects immediately with up to 5 attempts and then exponential backoff from 1s, while Scenario B (a disconnect after a confirmed Kraken trading-engine maintenance window) waits a MINIMUM of 5 seconds before attempting to reconnect, so TothBot does not hammer an engine still finishing maintenance [WS-REC-003]. On every reconnect the WS_Manager runs a full restore sequence (the ar:AR-056 mid-session restore path, which rule:HR-WM-016 keeps as a separate code path from cold start): it acquires a fresh WebSocket token, reconnects with the full WS-LIB connection parameters, re-subscribes every channel with identical parameters and parses each subscription-ACK warnings[] list, re-extracts maxratecount from the executions ACK to reset the operative rate-counter ceiling (never hardcoding 125, ar:AR-030), resumes the zombie-detection and 30-second ping keepalive tasks, restores the Position Mirror from snap_orders so no live position is left unmanaged after the gap, and restores the per-pair ticker event_trigger subscriptions [WS-REC-004]. Per the RR-SCOPE-010 confirm-absent check against live dv1_147, the other two GROUP 5 register entries — WS-PING-004 (a pong does not reset the zombie timer) and WS-ZOM-002 (track last_real_data_time using a monotonic clock) — were found already derivable from the existing rule:HR-WM-004 (reset on real channel events only) plus the dv1_144 WS-ZOM-003 time.monotonic()/last_real_data_time encoding, so they were not re-migrated. These facts are TothBot-organism (Kraken event-source) architecture per the binary test and are now derivable from the D1 diagram alone (DD-014); with GROUP 5 closed, the remaining D1 register gaps are the GROUP 1 connection/auth trio (WS-EP-003, WS-LIB-001, WS-AUTH-002) and the GROUP 2 candle-close fact (WS-OHLC-005). R holds at R10 (a <desc>-only edit).

A-31 (dv1_149) ★ Connection/Library/Auth Trio: WS v2 Endpoint Scope, the websockets asyncio Client, and the Spot REST HMAC-SHA512 Signing Model (DD-002 prose-follows-diagram for the D1 mod:WS_Manager dv1_149 GROUP 1 migration; TB00538):
The diagram mod:WS_Manager constraints <desc> is now canonical for the three GROUP 1 connection-establishment wire facts (SD-9-verified vs 0411001 dv1_13). ENDPOINT SCOPE: the general private/authenticated Spot WS v2 endpoint that carries executions, balances, order events, add/cancel order and openOrders/ownTrades is wss://ws-auth.kraken.com/v2, which is CURRENT and NOT deprecated; only the level3 (full order-book) WS endpoint moved to wss://ws-l3.kraken.com/v2 in the Kraken API change of 2 December 2025, and that change is scoped to the L3 endpoint alone — TothBot subscribes to NO level3 channel, so wss://ws-l3.kraken.com/v2 appears nowhere in TothBot's architecture [WS-EP-003; closes the prior uncited "ws-auth deprecated" note]. CLIENT LIBRARY: the WS_Manager connects with the Python websockets library's asyncio-native client, imported as "from websockets.asyncio.client import connect"; the legacy "websockets.connect()" entry point is prohibited [WS-LIB-001] — the connection invariants it is called with (max_size=10MB, open_timeout=10, max_queue=None, ping_interval=None) are already canonical at rule:HR-WM-002. REST AUTH MODEL: every Kraken Spot REST request, including the GetWebSocketsToken call that issues the pre-connect WS token, is signed with HMAC-SHA512 of (URI path + SHA256(nonce + POST data)) using the base64-decoded API secret; the 1 October 2025 Kraken authentication breaking change applied to Kraken FUTURES REST only, so the Spot REST signing model is UNCHANGED — the visible REST-API decoration already states the unchanged status, and this migration adds the signing construction a coder needs [WS-AUTH-002]. These three facts are TothBot-organism (Kraken event-source) connection architecture per the binary test and are now derivable from the D1 diagram alone (DD-014); with GROUP 1 closed, the sole remaining D1 register gap is the GROUP 2 candle-close fact WS-OHLC-005 (a Signal_Pipeline concern carried forward). R holds at R10 (a <desc>-only edit).

A-32 (dv1_150) ★ Candle-Close Signal-Evaluation Semantics: the Committed Candle Drives the Pipeline, the Forming Candle Does Not (DD-002 prose-follows-diagram for the D1 mod:Signal_Pipeline dv1_150 GROUP 2 migration; TB00539):
The diagram mod:Signal_Pipeline constraints <desc> is now canonical for the candle-close signal-evaluation rule (SD-9-verified vs 0411001 dv1_13 L323-326). On each 5-minute candle-close event — detected when a new ohlc(5m) frame arrives bearing a DIFFERENT interval_begin than the prior frame, which means the prior interval_begin's candle is now committed — the PREVIOUS, just-committed candle's OHLC values are the ones fed to ALL signal computations across the eight gates; the NEW candle (the current/forming interval_begin, still in progress) is NOT used in any signal calculation [WS-OHLC-005]. This is the live-WS analogue of the REST-seeding exclusion already canonical at rule:HR-WM-013 on container:Kraken_REST_API (GetOHLCData last/forming candle [-1] EXCLUDED, only closed candles seeded), and it lives on a DISTINCT component — the live candle-close signal path on mod:Signal_Pipeline — rather than the connection/channel layer of mod:WS_Manager, which is why it was carried forward from the GROUP 1-5 mod:WS_Manager cluster rather than bundled with it. The fact is TothBot-organism (Kraken event-source -> Signal_Pipeline) trading architecture per the binary test and is now derivable from the D1 diagram alone (DD-014); the Signal_Pipeline q1_do/q4_triggers previously stated only THAT the pipeline fires on candle-close, never WHICH candle's OHLC drives the computation, so the fact was genuinely absent in its codeable form before this migration. With WS-OHLC-005 landed, every one of the 37 TB00530 D1 register entries is now resolved (35 in-diagram across TB00531-539 plus the 2 reclassified-already-present at TB00537), so figure D1 Kraken_API_Connection_Architecture has reached FACT-LEVEL COMPREHENSIVENESS under the strict DD-014 from-the-diagram-alone standard: a coder can answer the five questions for every D1 component from the SVG + governs descriptors + figcaption alone. The DR-078 OPEN portion (D1 fact-level comprehensiveness) is thereby resolved, and 0411001 Kraken_WS_v2_Specification retirement (git rm --cached per CD-003) is UNBLOCKED — it is the SEPARATE TB00540 next-session primary (DEC-003 Path A / RR-SCOPE-011; not bundled here), to be preceded by the TB00511 cold-load precondition check. R holds at R10 (a <desc>-only edit; no visible <text> / geometry / viewBox change).

A-33 (dv1_152) ★ REST Connection, Authentication, and HTTP-Client Primitives: Headers, Nonce, aiohttp Session Config, Base URLs, and Per-Key Permission Scopes (DD-002 prose-follows-diagram for the D1 container:Kraken_REST_API dv1_152 CLUSTER R1 migration; TB00559):
The diagram container:Kraken_REST_API constraints <desc> is now canonical for the eleven CLUSTER R1 REST connection / authentication / HTTP-client wire facts (SD-9-verified vs 0411002 dv1_1; the first of six clusters in the TB00558 D1 REST-API Fact-Level Gap Register). AUTH: every private REST call carries three headers — API-Key (the TRADE key value), API-Sign (the HMAC-SHA512 signature per the already-canonical WS-AUTH-002 signing model), and Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded — plus a strictly-increasing integer nonce constructed as int(time.time()*1000); Kraken rejects any call whose nonce is more than 10,000 ms behind current time, so the VPS clock must be NTP-synchronized [REST-AUTH-003 / 004 / 005]. HTTP CLIENT: all REST uses a single process-lifetime aiohttp.ClientSession (the synchronous requests library is prohibited because it blocks the asyncio loop) configured with ClientTimeout(total=10, connect=5, sock_read=8) and TCPConnector(limit=10, limit_per_host=5, force_close=False) — force_close=False keeps HTTP keepalive so the TCP connection is reused across calls [REST-HTTP-001 / 002 / 004 / 005]. ENDPOINTS: both private and public REST use base URL https://api.kraken.com, private endpoints POST to /0/private/[Endpoint], public endpoints GET or POST to /0/public/[Endpoint] [REST-HTTP-006 / 007]. KEYS: TothBot uses two API keys whose permission scopes differ — the DATA key holds query-only scopes (Query Funds, Query Open Orders and Trades, Query Closed Orders) and MUST NOT be able to trade, while the TRADE key adds Create and Modify Orders + Cancel and Close Orders; both are stored on the VPS, never hardcoded, loaded from an environment variable or encrypted config at startup [REST-KEY-003 / 004]. These eleven facts are TothBot-organism (Kraken event-source) connection architecture per the binary test and are now derivable from the D1 diagram alone (DD-014); all eleven were confirmed absent from the live dv1_151 diagram-alone corpus before encoding (RR-SCOPE-010). CLUSTER R1 is the first of the six TB00558 clusters; the remaining 38 REST gaps (R2..R6) carry forward one cluster per session, after which a clean re-audit gates the DR-078 retirement of 0411002. R holds at R10 (a <desc>-only edit; no visible <text> / geometry / viewBox change).

A-34 (dv1_153) ★ REST GetWebSocketsToken and GetOHLCData Wire Contract: Endpoints, Request Bodies, Response Schemas, Token Validity, Startup Warm-Up Seeding, and the General-Error vs Rate-Limit Retry Paths (DD-002 prose-follows-diagram for the D1 container:Kraken_REST_API dv1_153 CLUSTER R2 migration; TB00560):
The diagram container:Kraken_REST_API constraints <desc> is now canonical for the nine CLUSTER R2 wire facts covering the two foundational REST data calls (SD-9-verified vs 0411002 dv1_1; the second of six clusters in the TB00558 D1 REST-API Fact-Level Gap Register). GetWebSocketsToken: a POST to /0/private/GetWebSocketsToken with a nonce-only body (TRADE key) returns {token, expires (seconds)}; the token is valid approximately 900 s, must be obtained fresh on every reconnect and never cached (the fresh-per-reconnect behaviour itself is already canonical at WS-REC-004, so only the 900 s validity value and the do-not-cache rule are added here), and on error it retries three times at 1 s and then HALTS startup and alerts the operator because no token means no authenticated private stream [REST-WST-002 / 003 / 004 / 006]. GetOHLCData: a GET to /0/public/OHLC with pair + interval=1440 (+ optional since) returns per-pair candle rows [time, open, high, low, close, vwap, volume, count] plus last, every field a string converted to Decimal on parse; up to 720 rows arrive, and after the already-canonical rule:HR-WM-013 forming-candle response[-1] exclusion up to 719 committed daily candles remain (~2 years); startup warm-up issues three calls per pair (interval=5 ATR seed, interval=60 EMA20/50 seed, interval=1440 initial regime) under the same [-1] exclusion and the same ar:AR-035 1.1 s staggering [REST-OHLC-002 / 003 / 005 / 008]. ERROR PATHS (the TB00558 R-D8 RECONCILE, resolved here): the GetOHLCData general-error path retries ONCE at 2 s, then logs OHLC_FETCH_FAILED and falls back to the prior regime without halting — this is DISTINCT from the rate-limit (HTTP 429) path already narrated at A-24 (retry up to 3 times, then stale regime); the 1-versus-3 retry-count difference is correct because they are different Kraken error classes, so neither value was silently overwritten [REST-OHLC-009 general vs REST-ERR-005 rate-limit]. CLUSTER R2 is the second of six; the remaining 29 REST gaps (R3..R6) carry forward one cluster per session, after which a clean re-audit gates the DR-078 retirement of 0411002. R holds at R10 (a <desc>-only edit; no visible <text> / geometry / viewBox change).

A-35 (dv1_154) ★ REST Reconciliation-Endpoint Wire Contract: GetOpenOrders, GetAccountBalance, and QueryOrders Endpoints, Request Bodies, Response Schemas, the Decimal Parse and portfolio_baseline_USD Assignment, and the DEGRADED-State Error Policies (DD-002 prose-follows-diagram for the D1 container:Kraken_REST_API dv1_154 CLUSTER R3 migration; TB00561):
The diagram container:Kraken_REST_API constraints <desc> is now canonical for the eight CLUSTER R3 reconciliation-endpoint wire facts (SD-9-verified vs 0411002 dv1_1; the third of six clusters in the TB00558 D1 REST-API Fact-Level Gap Register). GetOpenOrders: a POST to /0/private/OpenOrders with a nonce body (TRADE key, optional trades=true) returns result.open keyed by order_id, each carrying refid, userref, status, opentm/starttm/expiretm, descr, vol, vol_exec, cost, fee, price, stopprice, limitprice, misc, and oflags — every numeric field a string converted to Decimal on parse — and on error it retries once at 2 s, then logs RECONCILIATION_FAILED, alerts the operator, and enters DEGRADED state (monitor only, no new entries) because trading on a stale open-order book is an unmanaged-state loss event [REST-OO-002 / 003 / 006]. GetAccountBalance: a POST to /0/private/Balance with a nonce-only body (TRADE key) returns result keyed by asset (ZUSD, XXBT, ...) as strings converted to Decimal, the returned USD assigned directly as portfolio_baseline_USD (the spot/main-wallet-only restriction is already canonical at WS-BAL-002 and is not duplicated), and on error it retries once at 2 s, then logs BALANCE_RECONCILIATION_FAILED, alerts the operator, and enters DEGRADED state because sizing against a stale balance is a loss event [REST-BAL-002 / 003 / 004 / 007]. QueryOrders: a POST to /0/private/QueryOrders with nonce + txid + trades=true returns the GetOpenOrders result structure for only the queried order_ids (targeted single-order reconciliation), and on error falls back to GetOpenOrders for a full reconciliation [REST-QOI-002 / 003 / 005]. The three call names, purposes, and reconcile triggers (R-E1 WS-EXE-019, R-E5 WS-BAL-005/002, R-E9 REST drill_target/q1_do) were already canonical and were not re-migrated; all eight wire facts were confirmed absent from the live dv1_153 diagram-alone corpus before encoding (RR-SCOPE-010). CLUSTER R3 is the third of six; the remaining 21 REST gaps (R4..R6) carry forward one cluster per session, after which a clean re-audit gates the DR-078 retirement of 0411002. A-36 (dv1_155) ★ REST Emergency-Cancel and Status Wire Contract: the CancelAllOrders Kill-Switch Endpoint with its EMERGENCY-ONLY Use Restriction and Post-Call HALT, and the Status-API Scheduled-Maintenance Check (DD-002 prose-follows-diagram for the D1 container:Kraken_REST_API dv1_155 CLUSTER R4 migration; TB00562):
The diagram container:Kraken_REST_API constraints <desc> is now canonical for the seven CLUSTER R4 wire facts (SD-9-verified vs 0411002 dv1_1; the fourth of six clusters in the TB00558 D1 REST-API Fact-Level Gap Register). CancelAllOrders: a POST to /0/private/CancelAll with a nonce-only body (TRADE key) returns result.count, the integer number of orders canceled [REST-CAO-002/003]. Its use is EMERGENCY ONLY [loss-prevention]: because the call cancels every open order on the account, including the resting TP limit orders and the off-book emergency-SL stop orders, calling it in normal operation destroys crash protection, so it may be invoked only by a manual operator emergency action or an explicit EMERGENCY_HALT code path triggered by Bill, never by automation; it is specifically NOT the mechanism for normal MAE Layer-2 exits (those use cancel_order on the one position), NOT for the Full-Halt drawdown circuit breaker (that uses WS batch_cancel, which preserves the per-position TP and emergency-SL), and NOT for any automated routine operation [REST-CAO-004/005]. After any CancelAllOrders call the system logs EMERGENCY_KILL_SWITCH_ACTIVATED(count), alerts the operator at PRIORITY_CRITICAL, and enters HALT state; position state is then unknown and a manual operator review is required before restart [REST-CAO-006]. Status API: a GET to https://status.kraken.com/api/v2/scheduled-maintenances/upcoming.json on the Kraken Status page API (no API key, no nonce, issued on the same shared aiohttp ClientSession and timeout) returns an array of maintenance windows, each with name, scheduled_for, scheduled_until, and status (scheduled, in_progress, verifying, or completed) [REST-STAT-002/003/005]. For any window whose scheduled_for is within 2 hours of startup, the system logs KRAKEN_MAINTENANCE_SCHEDULED and alerts the operator at PRIORITY_HIGH; this is informational only and does not block startup (ar:AR-038), and on any error or timeout it logs MAINTENANCE_CHECK_FAILED, does not retry, and continues startup [REST-STAT-004/006]. The CancelAllOrders kill-switch purpose (R-F1) and the Status-API startup maintenance-detection purpose (R-F5) were already canonical in the visible figure and were not re-migrated; all seven wire facts were confirmed absent from the live dv1_154 diagram-alone corpus before encoding, the Status-endpoint URL having previously lived in section 2 prose only (RR-SCOPE-010). CLUSTER R4 is the fourth of six; the remaining 14 REST gaps (R5..R6) carry forward one cluster per session, after which a clean re-audit gates the DR-078 retirement of 0411002. R holds at R10 (a <desc>-only edit; no visible <text> / geometry / viewBox change).

A-37 (dv1_156) ★ REST Ticker 24h-Volume Wire Contract: the Public Ticker Endpoint, Classic-Pair-Name Mapping, the v[1]*p[1] USD-Volume Computation, the Startup-and-Periodic-Refresh Triggers, and the Instrument-Channel-Has-No-Volume HARD RULE (DD-002 prose-follows-diagram for the D1 container:Kraken_REST_API CLUSTER R5 migration; TB00563):
The diagram container:Kraken_REST_API constraints <desc> is now canonical for the ten CLUSTER R5 Ticker wire facts (SD-9-verified vs 0411002 dv1_1 section 4.8; the fifth of six clusters in the TB00558 D1 REST-API Fact-Level Gap Register). Ticker is the SOLE correct source of 24h rolling USD volume for the liquidity_24h cache: the WS-v2 instrument channel carries pair metadata only and NO volume, so reading 24h volume from the instrument channel is a defect (DEFECT-SS-006) [REST-TKR-001/010]. The endpoint is the public GET /0/public/Ticker?pair=[comma-separated CLASSIC pair names] (no auth, no nonce); WS-v2 symbols (BTC/USD) are mapped to Kraken classic names (XXBTZUSD) via the reverse map built at startup from the instrument-snapshot wsname field [REST-TKR-002/003]. Per pair the response v[1] is the 24h base-currency volume and p[1] is the 24h VWAP in USD, both numeric strings converted to Decimal; usd_volume_24h = Decimal(v[1]) * Decimal(p[1]) is stored in liquidity_24h[ws_pair] after reverse-mapping the classic key back to the WS symbol, with a pair missing from the response logged LIQUIDITY_PAIR_NOT_FOUND and EXCLUDED so Gate 2 blocks it (fail-safe) [REST-TKR-004/005/006]. It is called once for all pairs at startup during _warm_up_all_pairs() before SYSTEM_OPERATIONAL and then periodically every liquidity_refresh_hours (the 4h seed VALUE stays in section 9 per the binary test; the diagram fact is the periodic-refresh trigger), never on candle close; a single call covers up to 50 pairs as one request with no staggering [REST-TKR-007/008]. On a startup failure it logs REST_TICKER_FAILED, retries once after 2s, and on a second failure logs LIQUIDITY_SEED_FAILED, leaves the cache empty (Gate 2 blocks all entries, fail-safe) and does NOT halt; on a periodic-refresh failure it logs LIQUIDITY_REFRESH_FAILED and preserves the prior cached values; success logs LIQUIDITY_SEEDED / LIQUIDITY_REFRESHED [REST-TKR-009]. A cross-diagram drift was flagged and carried (CF-G2-VOL-FORMULA, NOT corrected this session): D2 gate:G2_Liquidity q1_do computes the figure as vol_24h * mid_price, which diverges from this canonical v[1]*p[1] (24h VWAP) wire fact and is the D2 side to reconcile (Gate 2 liquidity accuracy is loss-prevention-relevant). These facts are TothBot-organism (Kraken event-source) connection architecture per the binary test and are now derivable from the D1 diagram alone (DD-014); R holds at R10 (a <desc>-only edit; no visible <text> / geometry / viewBox change).

A-38 (dv1_157) ★ REST General-Error Taxonomy and Handling Policies: the error[] Success/Failure Criterion, the Six-Prefix Error Taxonomy, and the Invalid-Key / Service-Unavailable / Rate-Limit Policies (DD-002 prose-follows-diagram for the D1 container:Kraken_REST_API CLUSTER R6 migration; TB00564):
The diagram container:Kraken_REST_API constraints <desc> is now canonical for the five CLUSTER R6 general-error facts (SD-9-verified vs 0411002 dv1_1 section 5; the sixth and final cluster in the TB00558 D1 REST-API Fact-Level Gap Register). Every Kraken REST response carries an error[] array, and the single dispatch test applied before any result is consumed is REST-ERR-001: the call succeeded only if error[] is empty and a result field is present, and failed if error[] is non-empty. Each error string carries a leading prefix that classifies the fault -- EGeneral, EAPI, EOrder, ETrade, EQuery, or EService (REST-ERR-002) -- on which the handler dispatches. Three prefix-specific policies are now canonical: EAPI:Invalid key is logged CRITICAL with an immediate operator alert and is NOT retried, because a bad key cannot be cured by retrying and leaves TothBot blind and unmanaged (REST-ERR-003, loss-prevention); EService:Unavailable is logged WARN and retried after 5 s up to 3 attempts, then escalated as a maintenance condition (REST-ERR-004); and EAPI:Rate limit exceeded is logged WARN with endpoint and timestamp, backed off 5 s before retry, and escalated if hit more than 3 times in one session as a systematic over-use condition requiring CIATS review (REST-ERR-005). REST-ERR-005 is the general REST rate-limit policy and is distinct both from the WS rate-limit mechanism already canonical at ar:AR-030 / ar:AR-080 and from the GetOHLCData-specific HTTP-429 stale-regime path narrated at A-24, which the CLUSTER R2 REST-OHLC-009 entry only cross-references by label; its own WARN / back-off-5s / escalate-after-3 policy was not derivable from the diagram alone and is encoded this amendment. The never-swallow-errors logging rule (REST-ERR-006) was already canonical in the container q5_logs field and is not duplicated. All five facts were confirmed absent from the live dv1_156 diagram-alone corpus before encoding (RR-SCOPE-010). With CLUSTER R6 landed, all six TB00558 REST clusters are migrated and D1 REST is fact-level comprehensive for 0411002; a clean DD-014 re-audit (separate downstream session) zeroes the register, after which the DR-078-gated retirement of 0411002 unblocks (preceded by the TB00511 cold-load precondition check). R holds at R10 per the TB00453 bright line.

3. TothBot Trading Pipeline

The pipeline fires on every 5-minute OHLC candle close event. Synchronous and event-driven.
8 gates. Gate 3 (Regime Pre-Filter) new in dv1_5. Per-pair status check new in dv1_6.

NOTE — OHLC fires on trade events, not wall clock: If no trades occur after an interval
border, no message sent until next trade. Liquidity Gate ($500k/day) reduces this risk.
Same stall behavior applies to ohlc(60). TothBot must handle stalled system clock.
Addressed in 0511002 Signal Pipeline Specification.

3.1 Gate Summary 

  PRE-STEP: Parameter Store Snapshot Frozen (NEW dv1_5 — I-4)
    CIATS params captured as read-only snapshot at pipeline start. Consistent throughout
    full eval. CIATS writes applied only at inter-trade boundaries.

  PRE-STEP: Pre-Computation Cache Read (NEW dv1_5 — I-2)
    Hot path reads: regime cache | 1H EMA cache (ohlc-60) | ATR(14) running value |
    24h liquidity | per-pair status. Zero computation on hot path.

  ★ dv1_6: Per-pair Instrument Status Check
    Skip pairs in reduce_only, work_in_progress, delisted, limit_only,
    cancel_only, or maintenance state ★ dv1_12.
    Only online pairs proceed into pipeline.
    Prevents wasted rate counter. Full status list per 0411001 WS-INST-008.

  Gate 1: State Machine
    Kraken engine = maintenance or cancel_only: WAIT

  Gate 2: Liquidity Gate ★
    24h volume < $500k USD: SKIP → LIQUIDITY_REJECTED

  Gate 3: Regime Pre-Filter ★ NEW dv1_5 (I-1)
    TRENDING_NEG (any vol) or NON_DIR+ELEVATED: STOP → REGIME_BLOCKED
    Eliminates SSS computation on all no-trade regimes.

  Gate 4: 1H HTF Confirmation ★ (was Gate 3)
    1H EMA(20) <= EMA(50) for TRENDING_POS entries: SKIP → HTF_GATE_REJECTED
    Cache read from ohlc(60) WS subscription (NEW dv1_5).

  SSS Signal Engine
    Scores 5-min candle. Only reached if Gate 3 pre-filter passed.

  Gate 5: Selection Controller (was Gate 4)
    Signal fails any of 4 quality gates: SKIP → SELECTION_REJECTED

  Gate 6: Regime Gate / Sizer ★ (was Gate 5)
    NON_DIR+NORMAL: 50% position size. All NO ENTRY cases blocked by Gate 3.

  Gate 7: Risk Guard (was Gate 6)
    Drawdown halt / concentration / exposure. Pass or HALT.
    ★ Ticker-driven continuous drawdown monitoring between candle closes (I-7 dv1_5)

  Gate 8: Position Sizer ★ (was Gate 7)
    MAE = ATR(14) x 1.5x (incremental), emergSL = ATR(14) x 3.0x, TP = R:R formula.
    Never blocks — only sizes.

EVIDENCE BASE: 15-20% higher win rates with daily+hourly confirmation (5 independent
sources 2024-2025). Market Cipher: accuracy drops 65% in TRENDING to 45-50% in
NON_DIRECTIONAL. Break-even 40% for 1:1.5 R:R.

3.1 Gate 7 Risk Guard — Coder Detail Sub-Figure (Diagram 8 of 10)

Sub-figure elaborating gate:G7_Risk_Guard. Five sequential checks evaluated in strict order; first failure short-circuits. Each check shows the data inputs required, the pass/fail branches, and the event identifier emitted on failure. This figure replaces the architectural detail previously carried in 1011011 Risk_Engine_Coding_Spec (retired this audit cycle).

3.2 Gate 8 Position Sizer — Coder Detail Sub-Figure (Diagram 9 of 10)

Sub-figure elaborating gate:G8_Position_Sizer. A1 acceptance floor evaluated at gate entry (reject if expected R:R below the sacred 1:1.5 floor); then the sizing math computes MAE / emergSL / TP from ATR(14); the sacred 1:1.5 R:R floor is the only hardcoded parameter in TothBot V2 — never CIATS-owned. This figure replaces the architectural detail previously carried in 1011011 Risk_Engine_Coding_Spec (retired this audit cycle).

4. Exit Architecture — Ground Zero Redesign for Kraken

Rebuilt from zero for Kraken. Exit Controller owns all normal exits. Kraken off-book
emergency SL stop order is crash protection only. OTO evaluated and rejected (AR-008).

4.0 Canonical Identifiers (NEW dv1_37 — V-038.3 reconciliation per DR-042; DD-002 prose-follows-diagram). Architectural elements in §4 prose below resolve to the following canonical-token-form identifiers per 0311001 §15.11.3 type-prefix taxonomy: 

  layer:L2_MAE_Threshold      Layer 2 MAE Threshold exit (this section, 4.1
                              Three-Layer Summary). Encoded in D3 Exit
                              Architecture diagram across 13 SVG sites.
  channel:kraken_ws_ticker    Kraken public WebSocket v2 ticker channel that
                              feeds Exit Controller continuous drawdown
                              monitoring (this section, Layer 2 trigger
                              evaluation). Encoded in D1 + D3 + D6 SVG.
  rule:HR-PM-009              Position Mirror sole-writer architectural rule
                              (per 0511005 dv1_1 §HR-PM-009 + 0511004 dv1_3).
                              Witnessed by D3 + D6 SVG; Exit Controller
                              reads Position Mirror state, never writes.
  rule:HR-EC-013              Exit Controller cancel-then-sell sequencing
                              hard rule (per 0511004 dv1_3 §HR-EC-013).
                              Witnessed in 4.1 Layer 2 SEQUENCE CRITICAL
                              block below.
  rule:HR-EC-014              Exit Controller / Selection Controller state-
                              update authority via WS Manager (per
                              0511004 dv1_3 §HR-EC-014). Witnessed across
                              D3 + D5 + D6 wire-up callout decoration
                              groups.

4.1 Three-Layer Summary 

  Layer 1a — Regime-Based Exit:
    HTF regime reversal (EC-L1A-001) / daily regime downgrade (EC-L1A-002) / max-hold time expiry (EC-L1A-003). Step-1 pair-status precondition (AR-040); else WS cancel TP + market sell.

  Layer 1b — TP Fill:
    Resting TP limit on Kraken matching engine fills. EC cancels emergSL after fill confirm.

  Layer 2 ★ — MAE Threshold:
    (entry_fill_price - bid_price) >= ATR(14) x 1.5x.
    SEQUENCE CRITICAL: (1) cancel TP  (2) cancel emergSL  THEN  (3) market sell.
    CANCEL TIMEOUT FALLBACK (NEW dv1_5 — I-6):
      req_id registry tracks each cancel ACK. On timeout: check executions channel state.
      Confirmed cancelled: proceed. State unknown: retry once. Second timeout: ALERT +
      hold position + alert operator. NEVER issue market sell with ambiguous order state.
      Assign to 0511001 and 0511004.
    MPP RISK (C-1 dv1_4): market sell may reject on wide spread. EC MUST handle MPP
      rejection and retry. Assign to 0511004.

  Layer 3 ★ — Emergency Brake:
    VPS/TothBot/internet failure ONLY. Off-book emergSL stop order at ATR(14) x 3.0x
    on Kraken matching engine. NEVER in normal operation.
    MPP RISK (C-1 dv1_4): triggered market order subject to MPP on wide spread.
    Assign to 0411001.

4.2 R:R Formula 

  mae_pct      = ATR(14) x 1.5x / entry_fill_price  (CIATS-owned, uses ACTUAL fill price)
  net_loss     = mae_pct + 0.16% + 0.26%            (entry maker + MAE taker exit)
  net_gain     = net_loss x 1.5                      *** SACRED — hardcoded ***
  gross_target = net_gain + 0.16%                    (TP maker exit)
  emergSL_dist = ATR(14) x 3.0x / entry_fill_price  (NEVER in R:R formula)

  NOTE: All calculations use actual fill price, not limit price. OTO uses limit price —
  this is why OTO was rejected (AR-008).

5. Regime Taxonomy

Six-regime grid is foundation of CIATS regime-segmented analysis. Every trade tagged with
both asset_regime and market_regime (BTC proxy). Computed daily at 00:00 UTC.

5.1 Computation

DATA SOURCE (NEW dv1_5 — FLAG 2 — FP/DP VERIFIED):
Daily candles via REST GetOHLCData called once per monitored pair at 00:00 UTC.
Returns 720 entries. 

  CRITICAL dv1_6 (GAP-03): The last entry (response[-1]) is ALWAYS the current
  not-yet-committed candle. MUST be excluded from ALL calculations (ADX, EMA, ATR).
  Use only response[:-1]. Including the uncommitted candle corrupts all regime indicators
  and produces incorrect regime classification. See the Diagram 4 regime-engine visual / §5 + AR-017 (0711002 retired TB00596).

  Directional state:  ADX(14) + EMA(20) vs EMA(50) on DAILY candles (response[:-1] ONLY)
  Volatility state:   ATR(14) percentile rank in 50-day rolling window

  TRENDING_POSITIVE:  ADX(14) > 25 AND EMA(20) > EMA(50)
  TRENDING_NEGATIVE:  ADX(14) > 25 AND EMA(20) < EMA(50)
  NON_DIRECTIONAL:    ADX(14) <= 25
  NORMAL_VOL:         ATR percentile <= 67th
  ELEVATED_VOL:       ATR percentile > 67th

  asset_regime + market_regime (BTC/USD proxy) both tagged on every trade

ALL REGIME THRESHOLDS ARE CIATS-OWNED: ADX threshold 25, ATR percentile 67th, EMA
periods 20/50, rolling window 50 days — all starting values. CIATS validates each after
600 closed trades (100+ per regime bucket).

6. CIATS Architecture and Data Flows

CIATS is fully asynchronous. Never blocks the trading critical path. Reads only from
the Logger. Writes only to the Parameter Store. Deming PDCA governs every change.

6.1 Two Data Streams 

  Stream 1: EWMA Monitor
    288 candle evals/day. Valid at 50 evals (~4 hrs). lambda=0.2 [FP/DP validated dv1_6:
    half-life=3.1 evals]. Three monitoring signals:
      (1) rejection_rate_by_regime (F6)
      (2) rate_counter_by_pair from executions channel (A-1)
      (3) ws_roundtrip_latency_ms from WS response timestamps (A-3)
    MONITORING SIGNALS ONLY — never drives parameter changes.

  Stream 2: Trade Outcome Bus
    Fires on each position close. Captures: symbol, entry/exit price, hold duration,
    MAE reached, fees, exit reason, both regime tags, signal params at entry, actual R:R, P/L.

LOGGER — ASYNC BOUNDED QUEUE (NEW dv1_5 — I-5):
Logger writes go to an in-memory bounded queue. Queue size: 10,000 entries
[FP/DP validated dv1_6: 20 positions x 10 events/candle x 50-candle buffer].
Separate async writer flushes to disk. Logger NEVER blocks the trading hot path.
Queue must be bounded with immediate alert if queue fills. Assign to 0511006.

PARAMETER STORE — SNAPSHOT PATTERN (NEW dv1_5 — I-4):
TothBot takes frozen snapshot of all CIATS parameters at start of each pipeline eval.
Pipeline uses snapshot throughout. CIATS writes queued and applied only at confirmed
inter-trade boundaries. Prevents parameter inconsistency within single pipeline eval.
Assign to 0511002 and 0211001.

6.2 Statistical Thresholds 

  50 candle evals:       EWMA Monitor valid. Monitoring only. lambda=0.2 validated.
  200 trades HARD FLOOR: Inference valid. Proposal Engine activates. Half-Kelly activates.
                         SE(win_rate)~3.5%, SE(Sharpe)~7.2% [FP/DP validated dv1_6].
  600 trades:            Per-regime analysis. 100+ per bucket. MW power ~85% at alpha=0.01.
  Rolling 200-300:       Current performance window.
  Full corpus:           Zero-cost historical library.

  Mann-Whitney alpha (dv1_6) ★:  alpha=0.01 (one-sided). 99% confidence required.
  Spearman rho threshold (dv1_6) ★: |rho| > 0.3 AND p < 0.05 (both conditions).
  CUSUM parameters (dv1_6) ★:    k=0.5*sigma, h=4*sigma. Starting values.
  PDCA minimum interval (dv1_6) ★: Min 50 trades between any two parameter changes.

7. Complete System: One CIATS-Owned Organism

CIATS OWNS EVERYTHING EXCEPT 1:1.5 R:R: All parameters, thresholds, sizing decisions,
halt thresholds, multipliers, and trading rules are CIATS-owned starting values.

          ★ WS v2 uses underscore in stp_type values (cancel_newest). REST uses hyphen (cancel-newest).
          Never confuse the two. Different protocols, different formats.

          via mod:Long_Module or mod:Short_Module per dispatch seam (D7; mod:Short_Module
          labeled-group addition sequenced to M-4 per DEC-003 Path A).

          Long TP: resting limit ABOVE entry_fill_price (sell-side close above buy-side open).
          Short TP: resting limit BELOW entry_fill_price (buy-side close below sell-side open).

          dispatch seam.

          Long emergency SL: stop-market BELOW entry_fill_price (sell-side crash-protection
          exit below buy-side open).
          Short emergency SL: stop-market ABOVE entry_fill_price (buy-side crash-protection
          exit above sell-side open).
          Both directions atomic with TP via batch_add. Direction-symmetric per

  AR-047 (dv1_13) ★: Price and quantity rounding before ALL order dispatch. ALL rounding
                    MUST use Decimal.quantize() — NEVER math.floor/ceil. Float binary
                    representation causes precision errors (e.g. math.floor(0.3/0.1)*0.1
                    = 0.2 not 0.3). For exchange orders: any rounding error = rejected
                    order = failed trade = loss. Four mandatory rounding operations:
                    (1) order_qty: Decimal.quantize(qty_increment, ROUND_DOWN).
                        If result < qty_min OR result*price < cost_min: SKIP, log.
                    (2) entry limit_price: Decimal.quantize(price_increment, ROUND_DOWN).
                        Conservative: lower limit = more likely post_only fill.
                    (3) TP limit_price: Decimal.quantize(price_increment, ROUND_UP).
                        Conservative: higher TP = preserves net R:R at minimum.
                    (4) emergSL trigger: Decimal.quantize(price_increment, ROUND_DOWN).
                        Conservative: wider stop = more protective.
                    ALL Kraken API values (prices, qtys) received via WS or REST MUST be
                    converted to Decimal(str(value)) immediately on receipt.
                    NEVER Decimal(float_value) — inherits float precision error.
                    NEVER dispatch batch_add without pre-validated, pre-rounded prices.
                    A batch_add validation failure at Kraken kills the entire batch,
                    leaving an open position with NO TP and NO emergSL protection.

  AR-053 (dv1_13; amended dv1_43 — M-2 short-direction) ★: Per-module Pending Order Registry — capital commitment tracking.
                    Each trading module maintains its own Pending Order Registry

                    framework. No portfolio-wide commitment pool.
                    LONG MODULE — USD DEBIT TRACKING:
                      long_pending_orders: dict[str, Decimal]
                                        maps cl_ord_id -> estimated_USD_cost
                      POPULATE on long entry dispatch:
                        estimated_cost = order_qty × entry_limit_price × (1 + maker_fee)
                        long_pending_orders[entry_cl_ord_id] = estimated_cost
                      CLEAR on: exec_type=filled, expired, or canceled (long order).
                      HOLD on: exec_type=trade (partial fill — order still open).
                      Long Gate 7 USD check:
                        available_USD_long = long_module_wallet_balance
                                           - sum(long_pending_orders.values())
                        if available_USD_long < per_trade_USD_long:
                          SKIP_INSUFFICIENT_USD_LONG
                    SHORT MODULE — COLLATERAL HOLD TRACKING:
                      short_pending_orders: dict[str, Decimal]
                                        maps cl_ord_id -> estimated_collateral_hold
                      POPULATE on short entry dispatch:
                        estimated_collateral = (order_qty × entry_limit_price)
                                              / leverage_cap_short
                                              × (1 + maker_fee)
                        (leverage_cap_short = 3x starting per TB00000 v2_29 §9.17)
                        short_pending_orders[entry_cl_ord_id] = estimated_collateral
                      CLEAR / HOLD: same exec_type semantics as long.
                      Short Gate 7 collateral check:
                        available_collateral_short = short_module_wallet_balance
                                                  - sum(short_pending_orders.values())
                        if available_collateral_short < per_trade_collateral_short:
                          SKIP_INSUFFICIENT_COLLATERAL_SHORT

                    NOT consume short module collateral; a short pending order
                    does NOT consume long module USD. Module wallet balances

                    reconnect: snap_orders "new"/"pending_new" populate the

                              1011002 amendment).

                              retired TB00213; coding-spec re-creation deferred

  AR-054 (dv1_13; amended dv1_43 — M-2 short-direction) ★: Entry order partial fill + expiry/cancel — direction-symmetric protection.
                    A GTD post_only entry order can receive partial fills before
                    the GTD window expires or the order is canceled. When
                    exec_type=="expired" OR exec_type=="canceled" AND cum_qty > 0:
                    a REAL position exists at cum_qty units at avg_price fill price,
                    with NO TP and NO emergSL protection. Must be handled immediately
                    by the originating module (Long_Module for buy orders;
                    Short_Module for sell orders with margin position open).
                    CASE A (exec_type=="expired" AND cum_qty > 0):
                    CASE B (exec_type=="canceled" AND cum_qty > 0):
                      1. Clear the originating module's Pending Order Registry
                         entry for this cl_ord_id (long_pending_orders OR
                         short_pending_orders per AR-053 per-module routing).
                      2. Extract qty=Decimal(str(cum_qty)), entry=Decimal(str(avg_price)).
                      3. Validate qty >= qty_min AND qty*entry >= cost_min.
                         IF NOT VALID — DIRECTION-SYMMETRIC EMERGENCY EXIT:
                           LONG MODULE:  dispatch market SELL immediately
                                         (reduce position to zero from the
                                         partially-filled long stub).
                           SHORT MODULE: dispatch market BUY reduce_only=true
                                         immediately (cover the partially-filled
                                         short stub on margin). reduce_only=true
                                         flag mandatory per Kraken margin
                                         semantics — prevents opening a long
                                         position on the same pair if margin
                                         account were flat.
                         Log and fire CIATS (originating module's instance).
                      4. Recalculate TP and emergSL from actual entry price using
                         current ATR(14) and mae_mult / emergency_sl_mult.
                         Verify net_gain = net_loss × 1.5 (sacred R:R floor;
                         expected R:R direction-symmetric per AR-007 + AR-008
                         + TB00000 v2_29 §9.10).
                      5. Dispatch batch_add — direction-symmetric:
                         LONG MODULE:  TP limit BELOW entry + emergSL stop
                                       BELOW entry (sell-side both).
                                       WAIT — corrected: TP limit ABOVE entry
                                       (sell to take profit at higher price)
                                       + emergSL stop BELOW entry (sell to
                                       stop loss). Per AR-007 + AR-008 long.
                         SHORT MODULE: TP limit BELOW entry (buy reduce_only
                                       to take profit at lower price) +
                                       emergSL stop ABOVE entry (buy
                                       reduce_only to stop loss). Per AR-007
                                       + AR-008 short. Atomic batch_add same
                                       semantics as long.
                      6. Enter the originating module's Position Mirror with
                         cum_qty and avg_price (per-module position-tracking
                         per AR-053).
                      7. Log ENTRY_PARTIAL_FILL_PROTECTED with side tag (LONG
                         or SHORT) for CIATS regime-segmented analysis.
                    CASE C (exec_type=="expired" OR "canceled" AND cum_qty == 0):
                      No fill. Clear originating module's registry. Log. No
                      position opened. Same handling both directions.
                    CASE D (exec_type=="filled"): Unchanged. No partial fill concern.

                              1011002 amendment for direction-symmetric reduce_only

  AR-065 (dv1_14) ★: CIATS Kelly formula inputs MUST use net P/L from Trade Outcome Bus.
                    Kelly K_full = W - ((1-W)/R).
                    W = count(trades where net_gain_usd > 0) / total_trades.
                    R = mean(net_gain_usd for wins) / mean(|net_loss_usd| for losses).
                    Both W and R computed from Trade Outcome Bus realized net P/L data
                    (all fees included — entry maker + exit taker). NOT gross price change.
                    NOT theoretical R:R targets. For TothBot with 0.42% round-trip fees,
                    gross vs net R:R diverges meaningfully. Inflated Kelly from gross
                    inputs = oversized positions = excess loss on losers.
                    Negative K_full: log CRITICAL, alert operator, do not update params.
                    Assign: 1011010 CIATS-KE-006 through -009.
