  AR-067 (dv1_15; amended dv1_43 — M-2 short-direction + Path 2 long reconciliation) ★: SSS Signal Engine — direction-symmetric three-factor momentum scoring on 5-minute candles.
                    SSS is the signal engine that runs after Gate 4. It runs ONLY when
                    the pair is in a tradeable regime (Gate 3 passed) with 1H EMA
                    aligned (Gate 4 passed). Per the parallel-module framework
                    (TB00000 v2_29 §9.3), each module evaluates SSS against its own
                    direction-specific thresholds:
                    LONG-SIDE SSS (entered by Long_Module on TRENDING_POSITIVE
                    regime per HR-REGIME-007 M-3 amendment forward; until M-3,
                    long-only behavior preserved):
                      SSS PASS = ALL THREE conditions true simultaneously:
                      SC-SSS-1 (long): rsi_long_low (30) < RSI(14) on 5-min
                                       < rsi_long_high (50)
                                       INTERPRETATION: RSI in (30, 50) admits
                                       reversal-from-oversold setups with rising
                                       momentum. RSI > 30 indicates the oversold
                                       extreme is past; RSI < 50 indicates the
                                       setup is still in the reversal phase, not
                                       yet in extended momentum (which trades
                                       above 50 historically reverted in V1-era
                                       8-source 50/70 evidence base — this Path 2
                                       reconciliation per TB00180 SL §5 admits
                                       reversal entries instead of momentum
                                       continuation entries).
                      SC-SSS-2 (long): EMA(9) on 5-min > EMA(21) on 5-min
                                       Bullish short-term EMA alignment confirms
                                       the reversal has produced a momentum shift,
                                       not just an oversold bounce. EMA crossover
                                       is the bullish-confirmation factor that
                                       distinguishes a genuine reversal-with-
                                       follow-through from a dead-cat bounce.
                      SC-SSS-3 (long): current_candle_volume > volume_MA(20)
                                       × volume_sss_threshold (1.0x).
                                       Above-average volume confirms participant
                                       conviction on the reversal candle.
                    SHORT-SIDE SSS (entered by Short_Module on TRENDING_NEGATIVE
                    regime per HR-REGIME-007 M-3 amendment forward; M-2 sets the
                    parameter foundation, M-3 enables the regime routing):
                      SSS PASS = ALL THREE conditions true simultaneously:
                      SC-SSS-1 (short): rsi_short_high (50) < RSI(14) on 5-min
                                        < rsi_short_low (70)
                                        INTERPRETATION: RSI in (50, 70) admits
                                        reversal-from-overbought setups with
                                        falling momentum. RSI < 70 indicates
                                        the overbought extreme is past; RSI > 50
                                        indicates the setup is still in the
                                        reversal phase. Direction-symmetric to
                                        long-side SC-SSS-1 by mirror reflection
                                        across RSI=50.
                                        Naming: rsi_short_low=70 is the
                                        oversold-short equivalent (mirrors
                                        long-side rsi_long_low=30 by RSI=50
                                        reflection); rsi_short_high=50 mirrors
                                        rsi_long_high=50.
                      SC-SSS-2 (short): EMA(9) on 5-min < EMA(21) on 5-min
                                        Bearish short-term EMA alignment confirms
                                        the reversal has produced a downward
                                        momentum shift. Direction-symmetric to
                                        long SC-SSS-2 (inequality reversed).
                      SC-SSS-3 (short): current_candle_volume > volume_MA(20)
                                        × volume_sss_threshold (1.0x).
                                        Same threshold for both directions —
                                        above-average volume confirms participant
                                        conviction either direction.
                    All thresholds are CIATS-owned starting values per TB00000
                    v2_29 §9.16 + §9.17. Per-module CIATS instances own their
                    own parameters: Long_Module CIATS owns rsi_long_low / high;
                    Short_Module CIATS owns rsi_short_low / high. CIATS proposes
                    parameter changes after each module reaches its own 200-trade
                    inference threshold per TB00000 v2_29 §9.6.
                    SSS output: signal_params dict logged to Trade Outcome Bus
                    (per-module instance):
                      {rsi_14, ema_9, ema_21, volume_ratio, sss_pass, side}
                      side ∈ {"long", "short"} added for per-module routing.
                    Evidence base: long-side 30/50 + short-side 50/70 thresholds
                    are Path 2 reconciliation per TB00180 SL §5 (TB00179 chat-turn
                    12 ratification + 0811005 dv1_0 §4 mirror-symmetry comparison
                    table). The V1-era 8-source 50/70 evidence (TB00020 Search 1)

                    starting-value record; Path 2 admits the parameter shift on
                    mirror-symmetry grounds plus CIATS-owned-from-day-one principle

                    RSI-window + EMA-crossover + volume gating is preserved
                    intact for both directions; the entry philosophy character
                    shifts from momentum-continuation to reversal-from-extreme
                    (validation pending per-module CIATS at 200-trade thresholds).

  AR-073 (canonical: ar:AR-073) (dv1_15; amended dv1_43 — M-2 short-direction) ★: Per-side Selection Controller state management + pair_cache margin_eligible_flag.
                    WS Manager maintains per-MODULE state dicts (not pair-globally).
                    Per TB00000 v2_29 §9.6 per-module CIATS framework, each
                    module's state is isolated:
                    LONG MODULE STATE (WS Manager-hosted, per-symbol):
                      long_exit_cooldown_log: dict[str, float]
                                            — symbol → time.monotonic() of last
                                              long-side exit
                      long_consecutive_loss_count: dict[str, int]
                                            — symbol → consecutive losses on
                                              long-side without a long win
                    SHORT MODULE STATE (WS Manager-hosted, per-symbol):
                      short_exit_cooldown_log: dict[str, float]
                                            — symbol → time.monotonic() of last
                                              short-side exit
                      short_consecutive_loss_count: dict[str, int]
                                            — symbol → consecutive losses on
                                              short-side without a short win
                    Update on position close (per-module routing — long fills
                    update long state; short fills update short state):
                      Always (originating module only):
                        {long|short}_exit_cooldown_log[symbol] = time.monotonic()
                      If loss exit (MAE_THRESHOLD_BREACH, TIME_EXPIRY,
                        HTF_REGIME_REVERSAL, DAILY_REGIME_DOWNGRADE):
                        {long|short}_consecutive_loss_count[symbol] += 1
                      If TP_FILL (win on originating module):
                        {long|short}_consecutive_loss_count[symbol] = 0
                    All four dicts PRESERVED across reconnect (in-memory,
                    never discarded on reconnect). Per-module CIATS may reset
                    its own consecutive_loss_count[symbol] via PDCA parameter
                    update.
                    PAIR_CACHE MARGIN_ELIGIBLE_FLAG (NEW dv1_43 — short-module
                    prerequisite):
                      pair_cache: dict[str, dict] — symbol → pair-spec dict
                      pair_cache[symbol]["margin_eligible_flag"]: bool
                    POPULATION: at startup, the WS Manager queries Kraken REST
                    GetAssetPairs endpoint and reads the "margin_call" field
                    (or equivalent margin-eligibility indicator per Kraken REST
                    spec — exact field name to be ratified during 0411002
                    Kraken REST API Specification amendment, M-2 carry-forward).
                    For each pair in the monitored universe (D-03 USD+USDC+USDT
                    pairs passing AR-070 filters), the margin_eligible_flag is
                    populated TRUE if the pair supports spot margin trading,
                    FALSE otherwise. The flag is then cached in pair_cache and
                    read by Short_Module SC-GATE-1 short pre-gate (per AR-072
                    amendment above). The short-side universe is the subset
                    of D-03 universe where margin_eligible_flag == TRUE.
                    UPDATE: pair_cache is refreshed on mid-session WS reconnect
                      (re-query GetAssetPairs as part of the reconnect sequence)
                      AND on instrument-channel status changes affecting
                      margin eligibility.
                    Assign: 1011002 WM-SC-001 through -006 (long state),
                            1011002 WM-SC-007 through -012 (short state —
                              pending 1011002 amendment),
                            1011002 WM-PC-001 through -005 (pair_cache
                              margin_eligible_flag population — pending
                              1011002 amendment),
                            0411002 KR-AP-001 through -003 (REST GetAssetPairs
                              margin field — pending 0411002 amendment).

  AR-076 (dv1_16) ★: RSI(14) uses Wilder's SMMA — NOT standard EMA. Specification correction
                    to AR-068 which stated "EMA-smoothed" — that phrase is ambiguous and points
                    to the wrong algorithm. The correct RSI(14) incremental formula is
                    Wilder's Smoothed Moving Average (SMMA, also called RMA), with α=1/14.
                    This is distinct from standard EMA which uses α=2/(n+1)=2/15.
                    The two produce materially different RSI values (~5-8% variance).
                    A coder reading "EMA-smoothed" would likely implement α=2/15, producing
                    non-standard RSI that does not match any trading platform and would
                    systematically mis-fire the SSS SC-SSS-1 gate (RSI 50-70 condition).

                    CORRECT RSI(14) INCREMENTAL FORMULA (Wilder's SMMA):
                      Seed (first 14 candles):
                        avg_gain = sum(gains[:14]) / Decimal("14")
                        avg_loss = sum(losses[:14]) / Decimal("14")
                      Incremental (each subsequent candle):
                        avg_gain = (prev_avg_gain * Decimal("13") + current_gain) / Decimal("14")
                        avg_loss = (prev_avg_loss * Decimal("13") + current_loss) / Decimal("14")
                      RS  = avg_gain / avg_loss
                      RSI = Decimal("100") - (Decimal("100") / (Decimal("1") + RS))

                    For contrast — standard EMA (WRONG for RSI):
                      alpha = 2/(n+1) = 2/15 ≈ 0.1333  ← DO NOT USE FOR RSI
                      avg_gain = prev_avg_gain * (1 - alpha) + current_gain * alpha

                    STANDARD EMA IS CORRECT for EMA(9) and EMA(21) in SSS Gate 2:
                      EMA(9):  alpha = 2/10 = 0.2000  ← standard EMA, correct
                      EMA(21): alpha = 2/22 = 0.0909  ← standard EMA, correct
                    Only RSI uses Wilder's SMMA. EMA(9) and EMA(21) use standard EMA.
                    Do not conflate the two algorithms.

                    STATE STORED (unchanged from AR-075 — formula clarified only):
                      rsi_14_avg_gain: Decimal  (Wilder SMMA running state)
                      rsi_14_avg_loss: Decimal  (Wilder SMMA running state)

                    EVIDENCE BASE: 10+ independent sources across validation search
                    (TradingView rma(), StockCharts.com, Supra Oracle docs, Wikipedia,
                    LuxAlgo, AlphaRithms, Quantinsti, PineScriptMarket, Medium) all confirm
                    Wilder's SMMA (α=1/n) as the correct RSI formula. A 14-period SMMA is
                    equivalent to a 27-period standard EMA (2×14-1=27), not a 15-period EMA.
                    Validated TB00021, Search 4 and Search 10, 10+ sources.
                    Assign: 1011002 WM-SSS-001 through -008 (RSI formula corrected),
                            0711001 SSS-001 through -012 (RSI formula corrected).

                    SEMANTICS: The cancel_timeout_window defines how long mod:Exit_Controller
                    waits for a cancel_order ACK (exec_type=canceled from channel:kraken_ws_
                    executions) before triggering the cancel timeout fallback recovery
                    procedure (I-6 inspection-before-retry protocol per HR-EC governs in
                    0500000 §4 Layer 1a/1b/2 exit sequences).

                    FIRST PRINCIPLES CONSTRAINTS:
                      (a) Timeout MUST be >> typical round-trip to avoid false trigger on
                          legitimate network variation.
                      (b) Timeout MUST be << acceptable position exposure window to bound
                          the fallback recovery window.

                    OBSERVED SYSTEM CHARACTERISTICS:
                      VPS location: Ashburn VA. Kraken infrastructure: AWS us-east-1 or
                      co-located data center.
                      ws_roundtrip_latency_ms (A-3 CIATS signal — mod:CIATS_EWMA_Monitor
                      stream): typically 5-20ms under normal VPS-to-Kraken network
                      conditions.
                      cancel_order response path: TothBot → Kraken network (5-20ms) →
                      matching engine processing → executions channel push → VPS (~5-20ms).
                      Total: 10-50ms typical.
                      Network degradation (congestion, packet loss): adds 100-500ms.
                      TCP retry on packet loss: up to ~2-3 seconds.

                    DECISION RATIONALE:
                      5.0 seconds covers all realistic network disruption scenarios
                      (typical: 10-50ms, worst realistic: 3-4s) with margin. 5 seconds is
                      well within the 5-minute candle evaluation window. A false timeout
                      is recoverable (fallback verifies executions channel before acting).
                      A too-short timeout creates spurious fallback activations that
                      disrupt the exit sequence unnecessarily.

                    DERIVATION BASIS: VPS-to-Kraken latency characteristics in 0500000 §6
                    (A-3 monitoring), TCP retry timing (established networking behavior),
                    and fallback cost analysis.

                    CIATS ADJUSTMENT BASIS: CIATS starts from 5.0s and adjusts based on
                    actual ws_roundtrip_latency_ms data from A-3 EWMA Monitor stream per

                    SEMANTICS: The mpp_retry_count defines how many IOC limit sell attempts
                    mod:Exit_Controller makes at best_bid - 0.2% increments after a market
                    sell is rejected by MPP (Market Price Protection) — the C-1 MPP IOC
                    retry strategy per Layer 1a/1b/2 exit sequences.

                    KRAKEN MPP BEHAVIOR (ar:AR-035, 0411001 WS-MPP-001 through WS-MPP-004):
                      MPP fires when a market sell would fill at a price more than a
                      threshold below the current market price.
                      MPP is always active (no_mpp deprecated Sep 2025).
                      On MPP rejection: retry with IOC limit at best_bid - 0.2%.
                      Each retry uses a fresh best_bid from the most recent ticker bbo event
                      (continuous for open-position pairs).

                    FIRST PRINCIPLES CONSTRAINTS:
                      (a) Too few retries: position may not exit if spread briefly spikes —
                          position remains unprotected.
                      (b) Too many retries: position holds too long in adverse conditions;
                          each retry adds ~10-50ms latency.
                      (c) After all retries exhausted: HOLD + CRITICAL alert is correct.
                          A catastrophically wide spread requires human review.

                    SPREAD ANALYSIS on Kraken spot pairs in monitored universe
                    ($500k+ USD daily volume per decision:D-04 liquidity floor):
                      Normal spread: 0.01-0.05% for liquid pairs.
                      Elevated spread (news event, thin liquidity): 0.2-1.0%.
                      Extreme spread (liquidity crisis, circuit breaker): >2%.
                      Gate 2 ($500k min volume) significantly reduces exposure to pairs
                      with chronic wide spreads.
                      IOC at best_bid - 0.2%: fills within 1-2 attempts under elevated
                      spreads. 3 attempts covers near-extreme spread scenarios.

                    RATE COUNTER COST: each IOC retry = +1 add_order unit. 3 retries =
                    +3 units. Well within 125-unit ceiling per Kraken Pro Intermediate
                    tier (ar:AR-013).

                    DECISION RATIONALE:
                      3 retries at best_bid - 0.2% per attempt. After 3 failures: spread
                      is catastrophically wide. HOLD + CRITICAL alert is the correct
                      response. Operator must review. CIATS adjusts from first data.

                    CIATS ADJUSTMENT BASIS: CIATS observes the ratio of evt:IOC_LIMIT_FILLED
                    vs evt:SELL_MPP_EXHAUSTED (HOLD + CRITICAL outcome) across closed
                    trade records on the Trade Outcome Bus. High exhaustion rate signals
                    insufficient retries (CIATS proposes increment); near-zero exhaustion
                    with consistent first-attempt fill signals excess retries (CIATS may
                    propose decrement). Per TB00000 v2_38 §9.16 PARAMETER PHILOSOPHY +
                    §9.17 CIATS-OWNED PER-MODULE INSTANTIATED Exit controller block
                    (param:mpp_retry_count = 3 attempts starting).

                    five requires dv1_77 amendment per Phase 1 grep results).

                    SEMANTICS: On FULL_HALT declared by mod:Risk_Engine (rule:HR-DD-008),
                    mod:Exit_Controller issues a single Kraken WS v2 batch_cancel covering
                    ALL open entry orders (unfilled add_order outputs) and excluding all
                    resting Take-Profit (TP) limit orders and resting Emergency Stop-Loss
                    (emergSL) stop-market orders. Open positions remain monitored for
                    Layer 1 and Layer 2 exit conditions; Full Halt does NOT auto-close
                    positions — Bill decides on open positions.

                    KRAKEN BATCH_CANCEL BEHAVIOR (ar:AR-019, ar:AR-041, 0411001 WS-CAN-005
                    through WS-CAN-009):
                      batch_cancel returns a single count response (number of orders
                      canceled) — sufficient for Full Halt where per-order ACK tracking is
                      NOT required (no cancel-timeout-fallback dependency; no market-sell
                      sequencing dependency).
                      batch_cancel BYPASSES the rate counter maximum — critical when Full
                      Halt is triggered by a rate-limit scenario where the rate counter is
                      already saturated and individual cancel_order calls would be rejected
                      or queue-deferred.
                      cancel_order is the per-order alternative; used for Layer 2 MAE exit
                      cancel sequence where per-order ACK tracking IS required for cancel
                      timeout fallback (I-6 protocol per ar:AR-077).
                      cancel_order vs batch_cancel are NOT interchangeable per 0411001
                      WS-CAN-009 + 0511001 v1_9 WM-CAN-001.

                    FIRST PRINCIPLES CONSTRAINTS:
                      (a) Full Halt is a system-wide rate-limit or risk-circuit event;
                          rate-counter capacity may be exhausted at trigger time.
                          batch_cancel's rate-bypass property is the architectural
                          requirement that makes Full Halt operationally correct.
                      (b) TP + emergSL protect open positions. Canceling them during Full
                          Halt strips position protection — the opposite of Full Halt's
                          purpose (loss containment). Scope MUST be limited to ENTRY
                          orders only.
                      (c) Per-order ACK tracking is not required for Full Halt because
                          there is no downstream sequencing dependency (no market sell
                          conditional on cancel confirmation as in Layer 2 MAE exit).
                          Single count response is sufficient operationally.

                    DERIVATION BASIS: Kraken WS v2 cancel_order vs batch_cancel rate-cost
                    asymmetry (0411001 WS-CAN-004 cancel_order +8/+6/+1 by age vs
                    WS-CAN-008 batch_cancel cumulative cost AND WS-CAN-006 rate-counter
                    bypass), Full Halt trigger conditions (mod:Risk_Engine rule:HR-DD-008
                    drawdown threshold + ar:AR-019 multi-order cancellation requirement),
                    and Layer 3 emergSL crash-protection preservation invariant (ar:AR-001
                    Dead Man's Switch prohibition pattern — same loss-prevention property
                    of NOT canceling protective orders).

                    REGISTRY BINDING: §15.12.4 ar: registry entry — ar:AR-079 (governs:
                    rule:Full_Halt_batch_cancel_scope architectural decision). 0311001
                    v1_17 §15.12.4 ar: registry amendment deferred to a future housekeeping
                    increment per the established registry-gap-note carry-forward pattern

                    AR-078 precedent). dv1_77 preserves this AR-079 entry per DD-001 +

                    DERIVABILITY-TEST GATE — OUTCOME 1 single-compliant-option F
                    (Cloudflare AR-registration) surviving expanded-option-space
                    elimination including options NOT enumerated in TB00339 NSI §1.1
                    candidate set. Executed under RR-SCOPE-005 derivable-decision
                    execution authority.

                    SEMANTICS: Cloudflare's edge protection enforces a 150-connect-
                    request-per-10-min-per-IP rate limit on the public WS v2 endpoint
                    (wss://ws.kraken.com/v2) and the private WS v2 endpoint
                    (wss://ws-auth.kraken.com/v2). The limit is per-source-IP, applies
                    to NEW connection-establishment requests (WebSocket handshake
                    upgrade), and is enforced ahead of Kraken's matching-engine layer.

                    BREACH BEHAVIOR: When the 150-per-10-min ceiling is exceeded for
                    a source IP, Cloudflare returns HTTP 429 or actively blocks the
                    IP for the remainder of the rolling window. During the block:
                      (a) NEW WS connection attempts FAIL at the TCP/TLS handshake
                          stage with connection refused or HTTP 429 upgrade error.
                      (b) EXISTING WS connections continue to operate normally (the
                          limit governs connection establishment, not in-session
                          frames). Open positions remain protected by resting TP +
                          emergSL orders on Kraken's matching engine.
                      (c) If ALL WS connections are simultaneously severed (network
                          partition, VPS reboot, transient network event during a
                          burst-reconnect storm), the WS_Manager is locked out from
                          reconnecting until the rolling window decays — market data
                          flow halts and Signal_Pipeline + Exit_Controller cannot
                          react to new events.

                    LOSS-PREVENTION PROPERTY: ABSOLUTE. The 150-per-10-min ceiling
                    is the operational invariant that governs WS_Manager reconnect
                    orchestration. Per AR-056 (mid-session WS reconnect with
                    pipeline-no-fire clause; 11-step reconnect sequence DISTINCT
                    from cold-start) + per HR-WM-* reconnect-rate-pacing rules,
                    WS_Manager reconnect attempts MUST be paced to remain well
                    below this ceiling. Breach scenario (e.g., a reconnect storm
                    triggered by upstream network degradation) would lock out the
                    system from reconnecting for up to 10 minutes — during which
                    a flash crash, exchange status change, or position-level event
                    on a monitored pair could occur without market-data visibility
                    or pipeline-side reaction. Layer 3 emergSL crash protection on
                    Kraken's matching engine remains the ONLY position protection
                    during such a lockout (per AR-001 + AR-055 Dead Man's Switch
                    prohibition invariant).

                    FIRST PRINCIPLES CONSTRAINTS:
                      (a) The limit is EXTERNAL (Cloudflare/Kraken edge policy,
                          not CIATS-owned or TothBot-owned). TothBot cannot
                          negotiate, raise, or override the ceiling. TothBot's
                          obligation is to design reconnect cadence to remain
                          comfortably below 150 / 10-min / IP under all realistic
                          operational scenarios including burst-reconnect storms.
                      (b) The limit is PER-IP. The Hetzner VPS source IP
                          (87.99.141.44 per §11 STORAGE) is the single source IP
                          for ALL TothBot WS connections (both public market-data
                          shards and the private executions/order-state channel).
                          All connection establishments aggregate against the
                          single 150 / 10-min ceiling regardless of which WS
                          endpoint or which shard is reconnecting.
                      (c) The limit is ROLLING (not aligned to wall-clock
                          10-min boundaries). Each reconnect attempt consumes one
                          unit of the 150-unit budget for the next 10 minutes
                          from its timestamp.

                    OPERATIONAL HEADROOM ANALYSIS:
                      Typical reconnect cadence under normal operation: 0-2
                        reconnects per 10-min window (transient network events,
                        scheduled Kraken status events).
                      Worst-case burst-reconnect scenario: PATH 2 multi-shard
                        topology (per AR-070 amended + HR-WM-028 PATH 2
                        connection sharding) with N_conns = ceil(universe /
                        SYMBOLS_PER_CONN_SAFE) where SYMBOLS_PER_CONN_SAFE=500
                        per WM-SHARD-001. Universe ~500-700 pairs per D-03 USD+
                        USDC+USDT scope produces N_conns ~1-2 shards plus 1
                        private channel = 2-3 total connections.
                      systemd VPS-level restart cap: StartLimitBurst=3 /
                        StartLimitIntervalSec=600 (10-min window) per VD-SYS-008.
                        Caps TothBot process restart cycles at 3 per 10-min
                        window; each restart attempts to re-establish all 2-3
                        WS connections producing 6-9 connection attempts per
                        10-min window across all restart scenarios. Far below
                        the 150-per-10-min Cloudflare ceiling.
                      Pacing rules: WM-PACE-001 process-singleton token bucket +
                        WM-PACE-002 SUBSCRIBE_RATE_PER_SEC=10 govern in-session
                        subscribe frames, not connection establishment. Per-
                        shard reconnect spacing per WM-RECONNECT-016 transient-
                        WS catch + per-shard reconnect cadence provides
                        additional headroom against the Cloudflare ceiling.

                    DERIVATION BASIS: 0411003 dv1_0 §RL-MON-004 external-fact
                    statement (Kraken/Cloudflare edge policy documented from
                    public Kraken API documentation + Cloudflare published
                    rate-limit behavior on the wss://ws.kraken.com/v2
                    endpoint); §2.4 0500000 dv1_81 Cloudflare idle / 10-min

10. Six FP/DP Validated System Improvements

Derived from 80+ sources across 3 independent research passes plus 2 deep validation
sessions (144+ sources) plus 10-search Kraken validation [dv1_6] (126 sources).
5+ sources per parameter.

Finding 1: 1H HTF Confirmation Gate [TothBot]
Gap: No layer between daily regime and 5-min entry.
Evidence: 15-20% higher win rates with daily+hourly filter (5 sources 2024-2025).
Change: 1H EMA(20) > EMA(50) required for TRENDING_POSITIVE. Cache from ohlc(60).
Effect: Removes false signals during 1H pullbacks. Zero API cost.

Finding 2: ATR Dynamic Stop Distances [TothBot/Exit]
Gap: Fixed 2% stop ignores real-time market volatility.
Evidence: +15% performance, -22% max drawdown vs fixed stops (LuxAlgo + 4 sources).
Change: MAE ATR(14) x 1.5x. Emergency SL ATR(14) x 3.0x. Incremental (I-9).
Effect: Stop adapts to conditions. R:R formula preserved.

Finding 3: Regime Gate [TothBot]
Gap: Long momentum system trading in absent-edge conditions.
Evidence: Accuracy 65%->45-50% in NON_DIRECTIONAL (Market Cipher). Break-even 40%.
Change: NON_DIR+ELEV and TRENDING_NEG: no entry (Gate 3). NON_DIR+NORM: 50% (Gate 6).
Daily candles via REST GetOHLCData. CRITICAL: exclude response[-1] [dv1_6].
Effect: Stops trading when documented edge is absent. Pure loss minimization.

Finding 4: Minimum Liquidity Gate [TothBot]
Gap: No minimum 24h volume on asset selection.
Evidence: $1M+/day minimum for clean execution (Coin Bureau + 4 sources 2024-2025).
Change: min_volume_usd_daily $500k starting. Checked daily via ticker.
Effect: Protects fee formula. Ensures clean post_only fills and SL execution.

Finding 5: CIATS Half-Kelly Pathway [CIATS]
Gap: Fixed 5% sizing had no defined data-driven transition.
Evidence: Half-Kelly: 75% optimal growth at 50% less drawdown (MacLean-Thorp-Ziemba + 4).
FP/DP validated [dv1_6].
Change: At 200 trades: K%=W-(1-W)/R, apply 50%. Update every 50 trades. No ceilings.
Effect: Data-driven sizing replaces arbitrary fixed fraction.

Finding 6: post_only Rejection Monitoring [CIATS]
Gap: Rejection events logged but unused by CIATS EWMA.
Evidence: Rejection rate = direct signal of entry placement quality (Cube Exchange + 4).
Change: CIATS EWMA adds rejection_rate_by_regime stream.
Effect: Free diagnostic signal. Entry optimization pathway activated.

11.1 Normal Trade (Entry to TP or Exit Controller) 

  OHLC 5-min candle close fires on public WS v2
  Parameter Store snapshot frozen — all CIATS params captured (NEW dv1_5 — I-4)
  Pre-computation cache read — regime, 1H EMA, ATR(14) incremental, 24h liquidity (I-2)
  ★ Per-pair instrument status check — skip reduce_only/work_in_progress/delisted/
    limit_only/cancel_only/maintenance [dv1_12]
  Gate 1: State Machine — online or post_only: continue; else halt and wait
  Gate 2: Liquidity Gate — 24h volume >= $500k: continue; else skip
  Gate 3: Regime Pre-Filter — TRENDING_NEG or NON_DIR+ELEV: STOP; else continue (I-1)
  Gate 4: 1H HTF Gate — 1H EMA(20) > EMA(50) for TRENDING_POS: continue; else skip
  Signal Engine: SSS score computed on 5-min candle
  Gate 5: Selection Controller — 4-gate quality evaluation: pass or reject
  Gate 6: Regime Gate / Sizer — TRENDING_POS: proceed; NON_DIR+NORM: 50% size
  Gate 7: Risk Guard — drawdown/concentration/exposure checks: pass or halt
  Gate 8: Position Sizer — MAE=ATR x 1.5x, emergSL=ATR x 3.0x, TP=R:R formula
  Execution: WS add_order (limit/post_only/GTD 30-60s/cl_ord_id/stp_type:cancel_newest/deadline:now+5s)
  If expired/rejected: log reason code → CIATS EWMA monitors rejection rate. Done.
  If filled: WS batch_add → TP (resting limit) + emergSL (stop-market) atomic. cl_ord_id/stp_type:cancel_newest/deadline:now+5s
  Position Mirror records: symbol (key), entry_fill_price, qty, TP id, cl_ord_id, emergSL id
  Exit Controller monitors via ticker (continuous drawdown check — I-7)
  Logger records full entry via async queue. CIATS Trade Outcome Bus ready.
  TP fills: EC cancels emergSL. Or EC fires Layer 1/2 exit.
  Logger records full exit. CIATS Trade Outcome Bus fires with complete trade record.

11.2 Layer 2 MAE Exit (Adverse Price) 

  Exit Controller detects: (entry_fill_price - bid_price) >= ATR(14) x 1.5x
  WS cancel_order: cancel TP resting order
  WS cancel_order: cancel emergSL stop order (SEQUENCE CRITICAL: both cancels before sell)

  CANCEL TIMEOUT FALLBACK (NEW dv1_5 — I-6):
    req_id registry tracks each cancel ACK. On timeout: check executions channel state.
    Confirmed cancelled: proceed. State unknown: retry once. Second timeout: ALERT and
    hold position. NEVER issue market sell with ambiguous order state.
    Assign to 0511001 and 0511004.

  WS add_order: market sell (taker 0.26%)
  MPP NOTE (C-1): Market sell subject to MPP. EC MUST handle MPP rejection and retry.
  Logger: exit reason = MAE_THRESHOLD_BREACH
  CIATS Trade Outcome Bus fires

11.3 Emergency SL (Layer 3 — System Failure Only) 

  VPS crashes / TothBot dies / internet severs / unrecoverable WS disconnect
  Kraken matching engine fires off-book emergSL stop-market at ATR x 3.0x
  MPP NOTE: Triggered market order subject to MPP. Assign to 0411001.
  On restart: reconciliation detects closed position → Logger: EMERGENCY_SL_FIRED
  THIS IS A SYSTEM FAILURE EVENT. SHOULD NEVER FIRE IN NORMAL OPERATION.

12. Paper-Mode Dispatch Boundary Architecture

12.0 Architectural Status — First-Class System Element 

  PAPER IS THE MASTER. LIVE MIMICS PAPER.

  The paper-mode dispatch boundary is a first-class architectural
  element of the TothBot V2 system, on equal footing with the Kraken
  API connection architecture (Section 2), the trading pipeline
  (Section 3), the exit architecture (Section 4), and the CIATS
  architecture (Section 6). It is not a feature flag, not a code
  switch, not a deployment toggle. It is the seam at which the
  system's empirically-validated paper configuration physically
  diverges from live operation, and EXACTLY where it does so.

  This section codifies the boundary at architectural level so that
  every downstream specification (AA=04, AA=05, AA=06, AA=07, AA=08,
  AA=10) inherits a single, unambiguous reference for paper-mode
  behavior. Paper trading is the empirically-validated master per
  TB00000 v2_18 §4.4 PA-001..010. All Kraken WebSocket message-limit
  testing performed in TB00141 / TB00142 / TB00143 / TB00144
  STREAM 4 was executed in paper mode against live Kraken WebSocket
  infrastructure. Paper is what TothBot has been proven to operate
  against. Live mode is built to MIMIC paper wherever physically
  possible.

  ARCHITECTURAL ORIGIN. Audit chat 1 of TB00148 surfaced 24 unique
  defects in the deployed code at GitHub TothBot_V2-Code commit
  fb5de32. Cluster 1 (paper-mode dispatch seam undefined; findings
  09, 29, 30) revealed that the dispatch boundary was never
  promoted to a first-class architectural element in 0500000.
  Multiple Python modules called Kraken private WS send paths
  unconditionally, bypassing the WSManager dispatch gate. This was
  not a code defect — it was a specification gap at the architectural
  level. Bill authorized OPTION B Clean-Slate Rebuild on
  2026-05-04. This section is the parent of all 7 AA=10 spec
  amendments that follow in Phase 1 sessions 2-8 (TB00150 through
  TB00156). No downstream rebuild may proceed until this section
  is committed to TothBot_V2-Docs master.

12.1 PA-004 Permitted Divergence Points (Paper vs Live) 

  Paper and live operation MUST differ at EXACTLY the following
  four physical-impossibility boundaries, and at no other point.
  These boundaries are restated from TB00000 v2_18 §4.4 PA-004
  because every architectural decision downstream depends on them.

  DIVERGENCE POINT (1) — PRIVATE WEBSOCKET CONNECTION.
    PAPER: Does NOT connect to Kraken private WS. self._ws_private
           remains None for the entire session lifetime.
    LIVE:  Connects to Kraken private WS for order dispatch,
           executions reception, balances reception, snap_orders
           reconciliation, ratecounter monitoring, and ping/zombie
           monitoring.
    Why:   Paper places no real orders. An authenticated session
           in paper mode would create an outbound Kraken-facing
           connection that exists for no operational purpose and
           was never validated in TB00141..144 testing.
    Bind:  HR-WM-022 (0511001 dv1_5); PT-MODE-003 (0211005 dv1_3).

  DIVERGENCE POINT (2) — ORDER DISPATCH.
    PAPER: Simulates orders locally inside WSManager. No outbound
           order traffic of ANY kind transmitted to Kraken. Order
           methods (add_order, batch_add, cancel_order, amend_order,
           batch_cancel, dispatch_market_sell) gate at entry and
           return after logging a simulation event.
    LIVE:  Transmits orders to Kraken via private WS using
           _send_private().
    Why:   Paper trading by definition does not move real money.
           The dispatch boundary is the SOLE point at which paper
           mode protects operator capital from being placed at
           risk. Any code path that bypasses this gate violates
           PA-001..010 and is a session-halting defect.
    Bind:  HR-WM-023 (0511001 dv1_5); PT-MODE-005 (0211005 dv1_3).

  DIVERGENCE POINT (3) — CAPITAL LEDGER.
    PAPER: Synthetic spot_usd_balance starting at
           paper_starting_balance ($5,000 per module per D-05: long $5,000 / short $5,000). Updated by
           simulated-fill P&L applied locally using the SAME fee
           schedule (FEE_MAKER_PCT, FEE_TAKER_PCT) Kraken applies
           in live.
    LIVE:  Real Kraken spot_usd_balance from snap_orders / balances
           channel events.
    Why:   No real capital moves in paper. A synthetic ledger is
           required to give CIATS a P&L signal. Synthetic ledger
           uses identical fee arithmetic to live so paper P&L is
           shape-equivalent to live P&L. CIATS Half-Kelly
           computation operates on a unified corpus regardless of
           mode (PA-005 byte-identical CIATS data flow).
    Bind:  HR-WM-011 (0511001 dv1_5 baseline); HR-WM-032 (0511001
           dv1_5 ledger update); PT-MODE-004 (0211005 dv1_3).

  DIVERGENCE POINT (4) — POSITION MIRROR SOURCING.
    PAPER: Populated EXCLUSIVELY by the local simulated-fill path
           (HR-WM-033). No external Kraken event source.
    LIVE:  Populated by Kraken executions channel events and
           snap_orders reconciliation.
    Why:   No real Kraken position state exists for paper-mode
           strategies. Real Kraken positions held by the operator
           outside TothBot must not contaminate paper-trading
           Position Mirror state.
    Bind:  HR-WM-033 (0511001 dv1_5); PT-MODE-001 (0211005 dv1_3).

  EVERYTHING ELSE IS BYTE-IDENTICAL. Outside the four divergence
  points above, paper and live MUST execute the same code paths,
  same parameter values, same gate logic, same indicator math, same
  regime taxonomy, same exit decision logic, same drawdown formula,
  same alert routing, same logger output, same CIATS data flows,
  same reconnect logic, same universe population, same liquidity
  filter, same indicator warm-up. This is not a target — it is a
  hard architectural requirement (PA-005).

  NEW DIVERGENCE POINTS PROHIBITED WITHOUT BILL WRITTEN
  AUTHORIZATION. Adding a fifth permitted divergence point requires:
  (a) RR-SCOPE-009 four-question origin investigation; (b)
  empirical or first-principles evidence the divergence cannot be
  architected around; (c) PA-004 amendment in TB00000; (d) Bill
  written authorization. Until all four are satisfied, the proposed
  divergence is PROHIBITED (PA-006).

12.2 paper_trading_mode Flag — Definition and Lifecycle 

  paper_trading_mode is a single bool configuration parameter that
  selects mode at process start. It is NOT a runtime toggle.
  Switching modes requires a full TothBot process restart.

  CANONICAL VALUE.
    paper_trading_mode = True    -> paper-mode session
    paper_trading_mode = False   -> live-mode session
    Default if absent            -> False (live)

  LIFECYCLE.
    Authoring:  Bill manually sets the flag in the EnvironmentFile
                /root/.tothbot.env BEFORE invoking systemctl start.
    Read:       startup_sequence loads the config dict at
                process boot. paper_trading_mode is extracted and
                passed to WSManager.__init__ as the first
                consumer.
    Storage:    WSManager stores the value as self.paper_mode
                (HR-WM-021). Read once at __init__. NEVER mutated
                during operation. NEVER cached anywhere else.
    Logging:    First message emitted by Logger after startup is
                PAPER_TRADING_MODE_ON or PAPER_TRADING_MODE_OFF.
                Every subsequent log record carries the implicit
                mode-tag of the running process. CIATS Trade
                Outcome Bus records carry paper_trade: bool field
                derived from this mode.
    Termination: Mode persists for the lifetime of the process.
                 Process restart re-reads the config.

  WHY THIS DESIGN. A runtime-toggleable mode flag would create
  a category of defects in which simulated-fill state could
  contaminate live state or vice versa. Architectural risk
  asymmetry resolves to start-time-immutable: any operational
  inconvenience of restarting to switch modes is overwhelmed by
  the catastrophic risk of cross-contamination.

  WHO READS IT.
    WSManager:           Reads at __init__ via constructor argument
                         injected by startup_sequence. Stores as
                         self.paper_mode.
    Execution Engine:    Does NOT read directly. Calls WSManager
                         order methods. Per HR-EE-013, EE has NO
                         mode-conditional branching. Mode is
                         enforced at the WSManager dispatch
                         boundary (12.3).
    Long Module:         Does NOT read directly. Same architectural
                         pattern as EE.
    Exit Controller:     Does NOT read directly. Same architectural
                         pattern. EC's _close_position() close
                         sequence is mode-agnostic; WSManager
                         simulates or transmits the underlying
                         orders per the dispatch gate.
    All other modules:   Do NOT read paper_trading_mode. Mode is
                         not their concern.

  THIS IS A FIRST-PRINCIPLES SIMPLIFICATION. The flag is read
  ONCE, at one location (WSManager.__init__), by ONE module. Every
  other component is mode-blind by architectural intent. This
  eliminates entire defect classes (stale flag reads, divergent
  flag interpretations, mid-session mode flips) by construction.

12.3 The Dispatch Seam — WSManager as Sole Gatekeeper 

  The dispatch seam is the set of WSManager method entry points
  through which ALL outbound order operations MUST pass. WSManager
  is the SOLE gatekeeper. No other module may construct a Kraken
  order message and transmit it directly. No other module may
  call _send_private() on the private WS.

  GATED METHODS (the seam).
    WSManager.add_order()           Phase 1 entry order dispatch.
    WSManager.batch_add()           Phase 2 TP + emergSL atomic
                                    placement on entry fill.
    WSManager.cancel_order()        Individual cancel for MAE exit.
    WSManager.amend_order()         TP qty amend on partial fill.
    WSManager.batch_cancel()        Full Halt multi-order cancel.
    WSManager.dispatch_market_sell() Market sell for Layer 1a / 1b /
                                    Layer 2 MAE-threshold exit.

  GATE BEHAVIOR.

    PAPER MODE (self.paper_mode == True):
      Each method gates at entry, logs PAPER_<METHOD>_SIMULATED,
      schedules any required simulation task (e.g.,
      _simulate_entry_fill via asyncio.create_task), updates the
      synthetic ledger or Position Mirror per the appropriate
      paper-mode rule (HR-WM-032 / HR-WM-033), and returns
      WITHOUT calling _send_private(). Per HR-WM-023, calling
      _send_private() in paper mode is a session-halting defect.

    LIVE MODE (self.paper_mode == False):
      Each method constructs the Kraken WS v2 message per the
      relevant AR rule (AR-006 add_order, AR-007 batch_add TP,
      AR-008 emergSL, AR-018 amend_order primary, AR-019
      batch_cancel, AR-032 stp_type underscore, AR-033 deadline,
      AR-046 emergSL trigger, AR-047 Decimal rounding) and calls
      _send_private() to transmit. Returns after dispatch.

  CALLER CONTRACT.

    Every caller of any seam method MUST treat the method as
    mode-opaque. Callers do not know whether the method simulated
    or transmitted. Callers receive identical post-conditions in
    both modes:
      - On entry order add_order: a cl_ord_id is registered for
        callback. In paper, a simulated fill arrives via
        asyncio.create_task. In live, an executions message
        arrives via the private WS. Both result in the same
        ENTRY_FILLED log record and the same Phase 2 batch_add
        invocation.
      - On batch_add: TP and emergSL prices and order IDs are
        recorded in PositionMirror via WSManager helpers. In
        paper, IDs carry the prefix "PAPER_TP_" / "PAPER_SL_".
        In live, IDs are the Kraken-assigned values from the
        ACK. Both populate PositionMirror via the same
        pm.update_resting_orders() pathway.
      - On cancel / amend / batch_cancel / dispatch_market_sell:
        the post-condition is WSManager state mutation (Position
        Mirror, synthetic ledger, ticker event_trigger mode);
        the underlying transmission is invisible to the caller.

  NO DIRECT PRIVATE-WS ACCESS BY ANY OTHER MODULE.

    Execution Engine, Long Module, Exit Controller, Selection
    Controller, Risk Engine, Regime Engine, and all other modules
    MUST NOT:
      (a) Hold a reference to ws_manager._ws_private.
      (b) Construct a Kraken order JSON message and pass it to
          any send method.
      (c) Bypass the seam by calling private helpers on WSManager.

    ANY violation of (a)-(c) is a session-halting defect under
    PA-001 (paper is master) and HR-WM-023 (paper-mode dispatch
    isolation). The cluster 1 audit findings (TB00148 findings
    09, 29, 30) all instantiate (a) or (b) and are the originating
    defects this section is authored to prevent in the rebuild.

12.4 Synthetic Capital Ledger — Single-Owner Architecture 

  In paper mode the spot_usd_balance is a synthetic value
  maintained ENTIRELY inside WSManager. It is NEVER mutated by
  any other module. This single-owner pattern eliminates the
  distributed-write defect class identified in TB00148 finding 15
  (Position Mirror multi-writer ambiguity).

  OWNERSHIP. WSManager is the SOLE writer of spot_usd_balance in
  paper mode. WSManager is the SOLE writer in live mode also (it
  ingests balances channel events from Kraken and applies them).
  This is a paper-live parity property, not a paper-only rule.

  INITIALIZATION (paper mode only).
    spot_usd_balance = paper_starting_balance     # $5,000/module per D-05 (long $5,000 / short $5,000)
    portfolio_baseline_USD = spot_usd_balance     # captured ONCE
                                                  # at startup (HR-WM-011)
    Logger emits PAPER_LEDGER_UPDATED (event_type=INIT).

  ENTRY-FILL DEBIT (paper mode).
    On simulated entry fill at WSManager._simulate_entry_fill:
      entry_proceeds = qty * entry_fill_price
      fees_entry = entry_proceeds * FEE_MAKER_PCT
      spot_usd_balance -= (entry_proceeds + fees_entry)
      pos.fees_entry_usd = fees_entry  # required for net P&L on close
      Logger emits PAPER_LEDGER_UPDATED (event_type=ENTRY_FILL).

  EXIT-FILL CREDIT (paper mode).
    On simulated TP fill (FEE_MAKER_PCT) or simulated market sell
    (FEE_TAKER_PCT):
      exit_proceeds = qty * exit_price
      fees_exit = exit_proceeds * FEE_<MAKER|TAKER>_PCT
      spot_usd_balance += (exit_proceeds - fees_exit)
      Logger emits PAPER_LEDGER_UPDATED (event_type=EXIT_FILL).
      Control then yields to Exit Controller per 12.5.

  FEE PARITY. Paper uses identical FEE_MAKER_PCT and FEE_TAKER_PCT
  values to live. Live transitions to actual Kraken fee schedule
  per AR-012 baseline. Paper synthetic ledger arithmetic mirrors
  this exactly (PA-005).

  WHY SINGLE-OWNER. The TB00148 finding 15 root-cause analysis
  showed that Position Mirror writes from multiple modules
  (WSManager, Execution Engine, Exit Controller in pre-OPTION-B
  code) created a class of races and inconsistencies that no
  amount of locking could fully eliminate. The architectural fix
  is single-writer-by-design: only the module that owns the
  authoritative state may mutate it. WSManager owns
  spot_usd_balance. WSManager owns Position Mirror writes. Other
  modules READ via WSManager helper methods (HR-PM-009
  read-only-via-helpers pattern); they do NOT WRITE.

12.5 Paper Exit Routing Through Exit Controller 

  All paper-mode exit paths route through Exit Controller's
  _close_position() close sequence. The legacy parallel
  _fire_ciats_outcome path (dv1_25 era) is RETIRED. This is the
  cornerstone of paper-live CIATS data-flow parity (PA-005).

  EXIT FLOW (paper, all exit reasons identical pattern):
    1. WSManager detects exit condition (TP, MAE breach, Layer 1a
       signal, Layer 1b TP, emergSL price breach, time expiry).
    2. WSManager applies HR-WM-032 ledger credit.
    3. WSManager logs PAPER_<EXIT_TYPE>_DETECTED.
    4. WSManager calls
         exit_controller.on_paper_close(symbol, exit_price,
                                        exit_reason, fees_exit, wm)
    5. Exit Controller calls _close_position(...).
    6. Exit Controller emits TRADE_CLOSE log record with full
       P/L payload (entry_price, exit_price, qty, fees_entry_usd,
       fees_exit, net_pnl_usd, mae_pct_reached, vol_regime).
    7. Exit Controller clears Position Mirror.
    8. Exit Controller updates Selection Controller state (loss
       paths increment consecutive_loss_count[symbol] and set
       exit_cooldown_log[symbol]; win paths reset
       consecutive_loss_count[symbol] to 0; AR-073).
    9. Exit Controller releases BoundedSemaphore.
   10. WSManager._update_ticker_event_trigger switches symbol to
       trades-mode (no open position).

  LIVE FLOW (every step identical except origin of step 1):
    Step 1 origin: Kraken executions channel exec_type=filled or
    exec_type=triggered for emergSL.
    Steps 2-10 IDENTICAL to paper flow except no synthetic ledger
    application (real Kraken balances channel applies the credit).

  CIATS PARITY. CIATS log-file polling reads TRADE_CLOSE records
  identically in both modes. The TRADE_CLOSE schema is mode-
  agnostic. CIATS Half-Kelly (CIATS-KE-002), Mann-Whitney U,
  EWMA, CUSUM, Spearman, and Sharpe ratio operate on a unified
  trade corpus. The 200-trade hard floor for statistical inference
  (TB00000 §7) accumulates equally in paper and live modes.

  Bind: 0511001 dv1_5 §13.8 HR-WM-033; 0511004 dv1_3 §6A EC-PAPER;
        1011002 dv1_26 §16A.2 WM-PAPER-EXIT-001..005;
        0211005 dv1_3 PT-MODE-006.

12.6 Paper Telemetry Event Taxonomy 

  Paper-mode operations emit a dedicated set of structured log
  events that allow Bill, Claude, and CIATS to verify dispatch-
  boundary integrity. Live-mode events are unchanged.

  PAPER-MODE EVENTS (Logger event names).

    PAPER_TRADING_MODE_ON       Emitted ONCE at startup.
                                Tags entire log session as paper.
    PAPER_TRADING_MODE_OFF      Live equivalent. Mutually exclusive
                                with the above.
    PAPER_LEDGER_UPDATED        Every synthetic ledger mutation.
                                Payload: event_type (INIT |
                                ENTRY_FILL | EXIT_FILL), symbol,
                                delta_usd, fee_usd, new_balance,
                                exit_reason.
    PAPER_ORDER_SIMULATED       Every gated add_order call in
                                paper mode.
    PAPER_BATCH_ADD_SIMULATED   Every gated batch_add call.
    PAPER_CANCEL_SIMULATED      Every gated cancel_order or
                                batch_cancel call.
    PAPER_AMEND_SIMULATED       Every gated amend_order call.
    PAPER_MARKET_SELL_SIMULATED Every gated dispatch_market_sell.
    PAPER_FILL_SIMULATED        Generic event for any synthetic
                                fill produced by the local
                                simulation path.
    PAPER_TP_FILL_DETECTED      Synthetic TP fill (ask >= tp_price).
    PAPER_EMERG_SL_TRIGGERED    Synthetic emergSL trigger
                                (bid <= emergsl_price).
    PAPER_DISPATCH_BLOCKED      DEFENSIVE TELEMETRY. Emitted if
                                any code path attempts to call
                                _send_private() while
                                self.paper_mode is True. This
                                event MUST NEVER fire in correct
                                operation. If observed, halt
                                operations and audit the calling
                                module against this section.

  CIATS POLLING. CIATS log-file polling reads PAPER_LEDGER_UPDATED
  events to verify paper-mode capital evolution matches live-mode
  balances-channel evolution wherever physically possible. Schema
  parity between PAPER_LEDGER_UPDATED and live BALANCE_UPDATE is a
  PA-005 requirement.

  Bind: 0511006 dv1_2 §5.1 + §5.7 paper event taxonomy (parent spec
        is canonical post-1011007 retirement per TB00230 RANK 8 cascade).

12.7 Architectural Diagram — Dispatch Boundary 

  The dispatch boundary at architectural level. All upstream callers
  pass through WSManager seam methods. WSManager applies the
  paper_mode gate. Outbound traffic to Kraken occurs ONLY in live
  mode. All other system flows (public WS, OHLC, indicators,
  pipeline, regime, CIATS data flow) are byte-identical between
  modes per PA-005.

  KEY ARCHITECTURAL OBSERVATIONS.
    (1) The mode gate exists at EXACTLY one place (the WSManager
        seam). Upstream callers are mode-blind.
    (2) The simulation path and the Kraken transmission path
        REJOIN at Exit Controller. From there forward (Exit
        Controller -> Logger -> CIATS) the flow is byte-identical.
    (3) Every synthetic state mutation is owned by exactly one
        module (WSManager). No multi-writer races exist by design.
    (4) Paper-mode telemetry is observable (PAPER_* events) so
        Bill and CIATS can verify boundary integrity continuously.
    (5) The PAPER_DISPATCH_BLOCKED defensive event is the canary
        that confirms NO code path slipped past the gate.

12.9 Architectural Reasons This Section Exists 

  Three architectural reasons drove the authoring of this section
  as a first-class element of 0500000 (rather than as scattered
  rules across downstream specs).

  REASON 1 — Defect prevention by construction.
    The TB00148 chat 1 audit established that 24 unique defects
    were present in the deployed code at fb5de32. Cluster 1
    (paper-mode dispatch seam undefined; findings 09, 29, 30)
    arose because no single document defined the dispatch
    boundary at architectural level. Multiple coding-spec
    documents each made local references to paper-mode handling
    without a shared parent reference. Defects flowed from this
    fragmentation. This section eliminates the fragmentation by
    consolidating the architecture into one place.

  REASON 2 — Loss prevention takes priority over profit
    generation.
    Per TB00000 v2_18 §3 PRIMARY MISSION, loss prevention is the
    most critical mission function. The dispatch boundary is the
    SOLE point at which paper mode protects operator capital.
    Any specification gap at this boundary creates a class of
    catastrophic-loss defects (paper code dispatching live
    orders). Architecturally codifying the boundary at parent-
    spec level is the loss-prevention measure with the highest
    leverage in the system.

  REASON 3 — CIATS data validity.
    CIATS performs continuous improvement of TothBot parameters
    based on paper-trading data. For CIATS data to be VALID for
    live operation, paper and live MUST execute identically
    wherever physically possible. Any divergence outside the
    PA-004 four points invalidates paper-trading data as a
    basis for live decisions. This section enumerates exactly
    what may diverge and exactly what must not. Without this
    enumeration, the next CIATS-driven parameter change could
    rely on contaminated data.

  RR-SCOPE-007 NOTE. This section is constraint-additive. It
  does NOT narrow D-01 through D-08 LOCKED. Specifically:
    D-03 Universe = TOKEN/USD + TOKEN/USDC + TOKEN/USDT remains
         in force. The dispatch boundary applies to ALL pairs in
         the universe in both modes.
         AMENDED dv1_43 — M-2 short-direction: Short_Module
         universe is the MARGIN-ELIGIBLE SUBSET of the D-03
         universe (per AR-073 pair_cache.margin_eligible_flag
         populated from Kraken REST GetAssetPairs at startup).
         The D-03 universe definition remains in force for
         Long_Module; Short_Module operates on the subset
         where margin_eligible_flag == TRUE. RR-SCOPE-007
         compliance: this is constraint-ADDITION (a per-module
         eligibility filter, not a narrowing of D-03 itself).
    D-08 Top-N cap retired remains in force. No universe cap is
         introduced by this section. The dispatch boundary scales
         to whatever universe size the liquidity + status filters
         admit.
    D-05 Paper starting balance $1,000 remains in force as the
         legacy single-pool reference value (forensic record).
         AMENDED dv1_43 — M-2 short-direction: per TB00000
         v2_29 §9.4 operator-controlled wallet funding,

           paper_starting_balance_long_usd  = $5,000
           paper_starting_balance_short_usd = $5,000
         (Short paper wallet represents synthetic margin

  TRIADIC FAMILY ARCHITECTURAL ROLE.

  HR-EE-013 establishes behavioral parity (paper and live
  execute byte-identical code). HR-EE-014 establishes the
  parity-required surface (no direct private-WS access — all
  outbound order operations pass through the seam). HR-EE-015
  establishes the caller-contract discipline (mode-opaque —
  EE never reads paper_trading_mode or branches on mode).

  Encoding one rule without the others creates a governance gap.
  The three rules together establish that the dispatch boundary
  is the SOLE point at which paper and live diverge and that
